|  A comprehensive master report has been written to the artifact:
|   📄 **Pawtrackr Deep Scan & Core Architecture**
|   ──────
|   ### Key System Invariants at a Glance
|   1. Core Purpose:
|   Pawtrackr is a 100% offline-first, native Apple ecosystem (iOS, iPadOS, macOS) management suite and POS
|   designed specifically for independent pet groomers. It manages pet health and styling specifications,
|   active visit timers, point-of-sale checkouts with Bluetooth thermal receipt printing and cash drawer
|   triggers, client loyalty rewards, and business analytics.
|   2. Zero-Cloud Local Sovereignty (ADR-0005):
|   All data lives in a local SQLite database configured via LocalStoreConfiguration with cloudKitDatabase: .
|   none. Automated CI linting strictly rejects any CloudKit imports, push notification entitlements, or
|   unconfigured model containers.
|   3. Inferred Lightweight Migrations Only (ADR-0004):
|   Following the historical 1.0.2 migration regression (error 134504), SchemaMigrationPlan is strictly banned
|   in CI. All model changes must remain strictly additive (optional attributes, default values,
|   @Attribute(originalName:) renames), and @Attribute(.unique) is forbidden.
|   4. Financial Accuracy & Crash Recovery:
|   All currency calculations strictly use Decimal (no Double). In-progress checkout state is serialized to
|   lightweight off-thread JSON drafts via CheckoutDraftStore, while double-taps and payment retries are
|   rendered idempotent via CheckoutTransactionActor.
|   5. Disaster Protection:
|   Pawtrackr never deletes store files. Resets and restores create timestamped backup archives
|   (RecoveryBackup-*, PreRestoreBackup-*), and DataSafetyMonitor halts destructive wipes if client records
|   unexpectedly drop to zero.
| 
| 
| 
| 
| 
| ### The Trauma and Discipline of the 1.0.2 Migration Disaster
|   One of the most defining aspects of Pawtrackr's codebase is the historical scar left by version 1.0.2. In
|   that release, the team attempted to ship a staged SwiftData SchemaMigrationPlan built directly against live
|   Swift model classes. When existing 1.0.1 users updated, Core Data failed completely with unrecoverable
|   error NSCocoaErrorDomain 134504. Users were locked out of their salons' databases, and some resorted to
|   deleting and reinstalling the app, losing months of customer records. In response, the team permanently
|   banned staged migration plans via ADR-0004. Today, ci_pre_xcodebuild.sh scans every Swift file and fails
|   the CI build if migrationPlan: or SchemaMigrationPlan ever reappears. All schema updates must now be purely
|   additive (optional properties, default values, and attribute renames via @Attribute(originalName:)).
|   Furthermore, @Attribute(.unique) is strictly prohibited across all models because retrofitting uniqueness
|   onto an existing database that might already have duplicate records will crash SQLite on upgrade. Every
|   historical App Store build fixture (from 1.0.0 onwards) is stored in Fixtures and continuously verified by
|   StoreUpgradeRegressionTests.
|   ### The Reality of Pet Salons and the Total Rejection of CloudKit
|   Early in its lifecycle, Pawtrackr experimented with multi-device sync, as evidenced by residual tombstone
|   models like PresenceRecord and DeviceStatus. However, the team realized that real-world pet salons often
|   operate in environments hostile to cloud sync: commercial basements, converted mobile grooming vans, and
|   steel-roofed industrial units where Wi-Fi is spotty or drops out completely. Flaky cloud sync led to
|   synchronization collisions, battery drain, and checkout stalls while dogs were waiting on grooming tables.
|   Under ADR-0005, the team completely tore out CloudKit and committed to 100% offline local persistence. To
|   ensure cloud code never sneaks back in, validate_local_persistence.py parses the codebase during build time
|   and rejects any imports of CloudKit, NSUbiquitousItem, remote push notifications, or any ModelConfiguration
|   that doesn't explicitly state cloudKitDatabase: .none.
|   ### POS Checkout Resiliency and High-Speed Draft Serialization
|   The checkout wizard in CheckoutViewModel is engineered as a crash-recovery boundary. Grooming salons are
|   fast-paced and chaotic; iPads get dropped, cords get unplugged, or batteries run flat in the middle of a
|   checkout. To prevent lost work without locking the main thread, the app uses an isolated Swift actor,
|   CheckoutDraftStore. This actor offloads draft serialization to detached background tasks that write
|   lightweight JSON files to disk in under 5 milliseconds. Crucially, raw photo binaries are intentionally
|   omitted from these draft files to prevent multi-megabyte I/O stalls during step transitions. On top of
|   that, checkout idempotency is enforced by CheckoutTransactionActor, which checks an immutable transaction
|   ledger keyed on "checkout:\(visit.uuid)". If an anxious groomer double-taps the pay button or the app
|   recovers from a crash, the transaction cannot be double-processed or double-recorded.
|   ### Exact Decimal Currency and Proportional Price Reconciliation
| 
|   Pawtrackr strictly outlaws Double and Float for any financial state. In pet grooming, owners frequently
|   negotiate custom bundle discounts (e.g., offering a flat $85 on a ticket where individual wash, nail trim,
|   and ear cleaning services total $97.50). In CheckoutCalculatorActor, the reconcileLineItemPrices algorithm
|   handles these overrides by computing proportional price scaling across every item using Decimal arithmetic.
|   It then runs an exact integer-cent rounding distribution across the line items so that the sum of the
|   individual invoice rows matches the customer's negotiated total down to the exact single cent, eliminating
|   invoice discrepancies and accounting drift.
|   ### The Behavioral Psychology of the Additive Loyalty Engine
|   In LoyaltyEngine, loyalty points are bound strictly to the Client rather than the Pet (ADR-0002), allowing
|   multi-pet households to pool points across all their animals. More importantly, client tiers (Bronze,
|   Silver, Gold, Platinum) are derived exclusively from lifetimeEarnedPoints, rather than the current
|   redeemable balance. This embodies a deliberate behavioral psychology decision: a loyal client who redeems
|   1,000 points for a $20 discount is never punished by being demoted to a lower tier. The calculation is
|   completely pure, functional, and side-effect-free. Furthermore, to encourage frequent salon visits, the
|   engine automatically grants a 20-point bonus if the client rebooks within 45 days of their prior visit.
|   ### Native Hardware ESC/POS Receipt Printing and Cash Drawer Triggering
|   Rather than using generic print sheets or cumbersome vendor printer SDKs, BluetoothPeripheralManager
|   implements a custom CoreBluetooth driver that speaks raw ESC/POS binary directly to standard 58mm and 80mm
|   thermal printers over BLE. It automatically searches for common receipt printer service UUIDs (18F0, FFF0,
|   FFE0) and packetizes transmissions to prevent overflowing tiny printer buffers. Inside
|   ThermalReceiptPayloadBuilder, it formats itemized receipts complete with pet names, styling notes, loyalty
|   balances, and paper-cutting byte sequences (0x1D, 0x56). When a cash transaction is completed, it transmits
|   an ESC/POS solenoid pulse (0x1B, 0x70, 0x00, 0x19, 0xFA) directly over Bluetooth, popping open the physical
|   cash drawer automatically.
|   ### Defensive Storage Architecture and Anti-Corruption Zero-Data Watchers
|   Pawtrackr enforces an absolute non-destructive storage philosophy. Nothing ever deletes a SQLite store. If
|   a user resets the app or restores an earlier backup, StoreBackupRestore immediately moves the live .store,
|   -wal, and -shm files into timestamped quarantine folders (RecoveryBackup-*, PreRestoreBackup-*). Before
|   SwiftData even boots during app initialization, AppStoreBootstrap uses POSIX file locks via
|   StoreFileLockCoordinator to ensure no background threads or extensions touch the database while integrity
|   checks run. Once running, DataSafetyMonitor acts as a sentinel: if it observes the client count drop to 0
|   on a database that previously held data, it recognizes an abnormal detach or corruption event. It instantly
|   disables destructive UI actions, alerts the user, and presents a 1-tap restore prompt to recover from the
|   latest pre-boot snapshot.
| 
|   ### Media Budgeting and International Excel CSV Exports
| 
|   Because pet groomers take multiple before-and-after photos per visit, uncompressed images would quickly
|   bloat the local SQLite file to dozens of gigabytes and degrade performance. LocalMediaPolicy intercepts all
|   incoming photo data, downsampling full images to a maximum dimension of 1600px at 0.82 JPEG quality, and
|   generating 240px thumbnails for list rendering. On the data export side, ExportService generates CSV
|   documents for client and appointment books. It deliberately prepends the UTF-8 Byte Order Mark (0xEF, 0xBB,
|   0xBF) to exported files. Without this byte marker, Microsoft Excel on Windows fails to recognize UTF-8
|   encoding, mangling accented names like "José" or "Muñoz" and pet names with non-ASCII characters.
| 
|   ### The Sandboxed Practice Salon and Graceful Subscription Degradation
| 
|   To onboard new groomers and receptionists without the danger of altering real client history, PracticeSalon
|   spins up an entirely in-memory SwiftData ModelContainer seeded with realistic mock data (like Ava Martinez
|   and Milo the Golden Retriever). RootView dynamically hot-swaps the container at runtime while suppressing
|   system Spotlight indexing and notification scheduling. Finally, the app's monetization model in
|   EntitlementStore derives free-trial eligibility directly from Apple's StoreKit 2 introductory offers rather
|   than local device clocks. If a subscription expires, Pawtrackr refuses to hold the business hostage: it
|   falls back into a graceful read-only mode where client records, grooming histories, and CSV exports remain
|   100% accessible, paywalling only advanced Pro capabilities such as detached multi-window workflows on macOS
|   and loyalty program customization.
| 
| 
| 
| 
| Here are the additional technical insights, domain nuances, and architectural edge cases uncovered during
|   the deep scan:
| 
|   ### Staff Safety & The 3-Visit Aggression Clearance Protocol
|   In Pet.swift and Client.swift, safety warnings are treated with life-or-death seriousness. In a grooming
|   salon, groomers face severe bite risks when working with anxious or aggressive dogs around sharp shears and
|   clippers. When a pet is flagged with an "Aggressive" behavior tag, the codebase enforces an automated
|   safety rule: the aggressive warning cannot be cleared by a single calm visit. In
|   reconcileBehaviorTagsFromCompletedVisits, the system checks the pet's visit history and requires a strict
|   streak of at least 3 consecutive completed visits marked exclusively with calm or cooperative behavior
|   before the aggressive flag can be removed. If even one visit in that window is non-cooperative,
|   tagsRetainingAggressiveWarning forces the aggressive hazard badge to remain. Furthermore,
|   Client.hasAggressivePet bubbles this flag up to the main client list, warning the front-desk staff before
|   the dog even walks through the door.
| 
|   ### The SwiftData Decoding Trap: Transient Views over Raw Strings
| 
|   A fascinating architectural pattern in Pet.swift is how Swift enums are persisted. Normally, SwiftData
|   developers store Codable enums (such as Species or PetGender) directly as model properties. However,
|   SwiftData translates codable enums into Core Data "composite attributes". If a legacy database record,
|   corrupted store, or external import contains an unrecognized raw value in that column, Core Data will
|   uncatchably abort every single @Query fetch for pets across the entire app, crashing the process
|   immediately. To make the database completely crash-proof against decoding failures, Pawtrackr stores plain
|   strings in SQLite (speciesRaw, genderRaw, behaviorTagsRaw, preferredGroomingFrequencyRaw) and exposes
|   @Transient computed properties with safe fallbacks (e.g. Species(rawValue: speciesRaw) ?? .dog). The
|   @Transient macro is mandatory here to prevent the @Model compiler macro from synthesizing the crashing
|   composite attribute behind the scenes.
| 
|   ### Performance Optimization: External Image Storage & Indexed B-Trees
|   High-volume grooming salons accumulate thousands of appointments and photos over years of operation. To
|   prevent the SQLite database from bloating and degrading query performance, Pawtrackr applies two specific
|   storage techniques. First, in Visit.swift and Client.swift, all image data (beforePhotoData,
|   afterPhotoData, thumbnailData) is annotated with @Attribute(.externalStorage). SwiftData strips these large
|   binary blobs out of the database table, saving them as discrete files in the app's support directory and
|   keeping SQLite B-Tree nodes compact and fast. Second, Client.swift declares a composite database index:
|   #Index<Client>([\.lastName, \.firstName], [\.lastVisitDate], [\.phoneDigits], [\.normalizedNameKey],
|   [\.searchKeysVersion]). Instead of executing expensive full-table scans with case-insensitive string
|   matching, the app automatically maintains phoneDigits (a digits-only string that allows matching 5551234
|   against formatted numbers like (555) 123-4...) and normalizedNameKey (diacritic-folded lowercase names),
|   ensuring instant-as-you-type search performance even on huge client catalogs.
|   ### Multi-Window Desktop Power on macOS & "Pawtrackr Pulse"
|   Pawtrackr is not a scaled-up mobile app; it is deeply optimized for macOS and Mac Catalyst in
|   PawtrackrApp.swift. It introduces DetachedClientWindow and DetachedInsightsWindow, allowing salon
|   receptionists on an iMac or MacBook to pop open dedicated floating windows for specific client files or
|   live financial reports while keeping the appointment calendar open. It registers full native macOS keyboard
|   shortcuts (⌘1 Dashboard, ⌘2 Clients, ⌘3 Visits, ⌘4 Settings, ⌘I Insights, ⌘F Find Clients, ⌘, Preferences).
|   Most notably, it features a native macOS MenuBarExtra called Pawtrackr Pulse, giving groomers a persistent
|   menu bar icon (pawprint.circle.fill) where they can peek at active grooming timers, today's schedule, and
|   quick salon stats without having to switch focus away from their current workspace.
| 
|   ### Keychain-Hardened Anti-Tamper PIN Lockout
|   The staff authentication layer in PinLockView.swift features a defensive security implementation against
|   salon tablet tampering. While it supports Face ID and Touch ID via BiometricAuthenticator, employees
|   frequently unlock the device with a 4-digit PIN. To stop someone from brute-forcing the PIN, the failed
|   attempt counter and lockout cooldown deadline are stored directly in the Apple Keychain via
|   PinLockoutGuard. This means if someone gets locked out, force-quitting or restarting the app does not reset
|   the counter; when reopened, the app checks the keychain and resumes the cooldown countdown timer.
|   Furthermore, when the app enters the background or App Switcher, PrivacyScreen immediately blanks the
|   screen with a blur material to prevent sensitive client phone numbers or daily revenue figures from
|   lingering in system multitasking snapshots.
|   ### Privacy-Governed Spotlight Search Integration
| 
|   In SpotlightIndexer.swift, Pawtrackr integrates with iOS and macOS CoreSpotlight, letting salon owners
|   search for client names and pet breeds directly from the system home screen. However, this feature is
|   strictly governed by the app's privacy policy: the moment a salon owner enables the PIN or biometric App
|   Lock, SpotlightIndexer acquires an internal lock and purges all indexed client and pet records from the OS
|   index. This guarantees that an authorized user cannot pick up the salon's iPad and search client records
|   from the iOS lock screen or Spotlight search bar. Additionally, live edits are buffered and debounced with
|   a 500-millisecond window per entity ID to ensure rapid typing in notes fields does not flood the OS
|   indexing daemon.
| 
|   ### One-Tap Client Communication via SMS & WhatsApp
| 
|   In CommunicationSheet.swift, the app automates customer communication for busy groomers. It provides pre-
|   seeded templates with dynamic placeholder substitution ({pet_name}, {client_name}, {salon_name}) for common
|   operational scenarios: "Ready for Pickup", "Appointment Reminder", "Running Late", and "Post-Groom Follow-
|   up". Once selected, groomers can adjust the message within safety character limits and send it with a
|   single tap using native SMS or WhatsApp URL schemes (whatsapp://send), eliminating the friction of manual
|   dialing or re-typing numbers during busy salon hours.
| 
|   ### Fail-Safe StoreKit Timeout Handling
| 
|   In EntitlementStore.swift, the team engineered a workaround for an elusive StoreKit 2 pitfall: on spotty
|   salon Wi-Fi, Apple's Product.products(for:) request can hang indefinitely without throwing an error,
|   leaving the subscription paywall stuck in a perpetual loading state. To resolve this, Pawtrackr implements
|   StoreKitTimeout, which executes product lookups inside an asynchronous throwing task group with a strict 2-
|   second wall-clock deadline. If StoreKit fails to respond within 2 seconds, the task group throws a
|   localized timeout error, breaks the spinner, and presents a retry option, guaranteeing that network delays
|   never lock up the user interface.
| 
|   ### The "Transformation" Before-and-After Showcase
| 
|   Recognizing the visual appeal of grooming results, TransformationView.swift dynamically pairs the visit's
|   before and after photos into a side-by-side comparison card. Groomers can open this view upon visit
|   completion and use a native ShareLink to generate a pre-formatted social media post ("Check out Milo's
|   grooming transformation at Pawtrackr!"), turning routine visits into organic referral marketing for the
|   salon.
|

|   ### Staff Safety & The 3-Visit Aggression Clearance Protocol
|   In Pet.swift and Client.swift, safety warnings are treated with life-or-death seriousness. In a grooming
|   salon, groomers face severe bite risks when working with anxious or aggressive dogs around sharp shears and
|   clippers. When a pet is flagged with an "Aggressive" behavior tag, the codebase enforces an automated
|   safety rule: the aggressive warning cannot be cleared by a single calm visit. In
|   reconcileBehaviorTagsFromCompletedVisits, the system checks the pet's visit history and requires a strict
|   streak of at least 3 consecutive completed visits marked exclusively with calm or cooperative behavior
|   before the aggressive flag can be removed. If even one visit in that window is non-cooperative,
|   tagsRetainingAggressiveWarning forces the aggressive hazard badge to remain. Furthermore,
|   Client.hasAggressivePet bubbles this flag up to the main client list, warning the front-desk staff before
|   the dog even walks through the door.
| 
|   ### The SwiftData Decoding Trap: Transient Views over Raw Strings
| 
|   A fascinating architectural pattern in Pet.swift is how Swift enums are persisted. Normally, SwiftData
|   developers store Codable enums (such as Species or PetGender) directly as model properties. However,
|   SwiftData translates codable enums into Core Data "composite attributes". If a legacy database record,
|   corrupted store, or external import contains an unrecognized raw value in that column, Core Data will
|   uncatchably abort every single @Query fetch for pets across the entire app, crashing the process
|   immediately. To make the database completely crash-proof against decoding failures, Pawtrackr stores plain
|   strings in SQLite (speciesRaw, genderRaw, behaviorTagsRaw, preferredGroomingFrequencyRaw) and exposes
|   @Transient computed properties with safe fallbacks (e.g. Species(rawValue: speciesRaw) ?? .dog). The
|   @Transient macro is mandatory here to prevent the @Model compiler macro from synthesizing the crashing
|   composite attribute behind the scenes.
| 
|   ### Performance Optimization: External Image Storage & Indexed B-Trees
|   High-volume grooming salons accumulate thousands of appointments and photos over years of operation. To
|   prevent the SQLite database from bloating and degrading query performance, Pawtrackr applies two specific
|   storage techniques. First, in Visit.swift and Client.swift, all image data (beforePhotoData,
|   afterPhotoData, thumbnailData) is annotated with @Attribute(.externalStorage). SwiftData strips these large
|   binary blobs out of the database table, saving them as discrete files in the app's support directory and
|   keeping SQLite B-Tree nodes compact and fast. Second, Client.swift declares a composite database index:
|   #Index<Client>([\.lastName, \.firstName], [\.lastVisitDate], [\.phoneDigits], [\.normalizedNameKey],
|   [\.searchKeysVersion]). Instead of executing expensive full-table scans with case-insensitive string
|   matching, the app automatically maintains phoneDigits (a digits-only string that allows matching 5551234
|   against formatted numbers like (555) 123-4...) and normalizedNameKey (diacritic-folded lowercase names),
|   ensuring instant-as-you-type search performance even on huge client catalogs.

|   Here are more deep technical learnings, domain-specific edge cases, and architectural safeguards uncovered
|   in the codebase:
|   ### Intelligent Edit Conflict Resolution Without Silent Overwrites
|   In ClientEditConflict.swift, the team designed a concurrent-editing safeguard for busy salons where
|   multiple staff members might view or edit the same client profile simultaneously. When a groomer opens an
|   edit sheet, the app captures a ClientEditBaseline snapshot (updatedAt, lastModifiedBy, and exact field
|   values). When saving, ClientEditSaver fetches a fresh copy of the record from a detached context. If
|   another user or device modified the record while the sheet was open, it halts the save and flags
|   .changedElsewhere. Crucially, rather than blindly overwriting or throwing away data, the saver computes
|   field-level deltas: it only updates the specific fields the groomer modified on top of the newly fetched
|   record. For instance, if another receptionist added an email address while this groomer was updating the
|   phone number, saving the phone number will not silently wipe the new email address.
|   ### The Missing Information Sentinel & Front-Desk Intake Hygiene
|   In ClientMissingInfo.swift, Pawtrackr provides a continuous record audit engine for front-desk
|   receptionists. A pet salon frequently deals with incomplete intake forms during walk-ins. The system
|   continually evaluates client records against critical operational criteria: missing secondary emergency
|   contacts, empty phone numbers, or absent email addresses. When a profile is incomplete, the system formats
|   localized badges (such as "Missing: Emergency contact and Owner email") and surfaces a dynamic filter chip
|   across the client directory. This allows staff during morning drop-offs to tap a single filter button,
|   instantly isolate every client with missing contact details, and collect emergency phone numbers before the
|   owner drives away.
|   ### Automated Background Maintenance & The Non-Destructive Photo Rule
|   In ScheduledTasks.swift, Pawtrackr integrates with Apple's BackgroundTasks framework
|   (PartnerShipWithMedia.Pawtrackr.maintenance) to execute weekly maintenance (targeting Sunday mornings at
|   3:00 AM, with fallback on app launch). This task rebuilds daily revenue summaries and triggers storage
|   optimizations via DataPruner. What is remarkable is the explicit philosophy hardcoded into
|   DataPruner.swift:24-27: by default, it deliberately refuses to delete historical visit photos, logging that
|   "visit photos are stored user data, not a disposable cache." In professional pet grooming, before-and-after
|   photos serve as legal and medical protection against disputes (proving coat matting, skin irritations, or
|   pre-existing injuries before the pet was touched). Furthermore, maintenance checks against
|   SystemWorkloadPolicy: if the device is on Low Power Mode or undergoing thermal throttling, heavy
|   maintenance automatically defers itself to preserve battery and performance.
|   ### Ambient Mesh Gradients & Force Touch Trackpad Haptics
| 
|   The UI layer is crafted using modern Apple design patterns. In MeshGradientView.swift, the app leverages
|   the iOS 18 / macOS 15 native MeshGradient API with a 3×3 coordinate matrix. It runs an ambient timer that
|   sinusoidally modulates the center control point ([0.5 + sin(time) * 0.1, 0.5 + cos(time) * 0.1]), creating
|   an organic, fluid glassmorphic background that animates smoothly behind cards. In HapticManager.swift,
|   tactile feedback is not limited to iOS iPhones with Taptic Engines; it bridges directly into macOS AppKit
|   using NSHapticFeedbackManager. When a groomer clicks buttons or toggles filters on a MacBook or Magic
|   Trackpad, the Force Touch trackpad physically clicks with .alignment and .levelChange actuator pulses.
| 
|   ### Celtic & Compound Name Typography Normalization
| 
|   In String+Extensions.swift, the app includes domain-tailored name formatting. Standard Swift .capitalized
|   mangles names with apostrophes or hyphens (turning "o'brien" into "O'brien" and dropping internal casing).
|   Pawtrackr implements custom capitalizedName logic that identifies Celtic and Gaelic prefixes (e.g.,
|   automatically converting "o'brien" to "O'Brien") and splits hyphenated family names (e.g., "smith-jones" to
|   "Smith-Jones"). In addition, TextInputLimits establishes hard-bounded sanitization across all input fields
|   (names capped at 64 characters, phone numbers at 32, emails at 254, notes at 1,000), preventing layout
|   clipping and database memory exhaustion from pasted text.
| 
|   ### Reversible Sample Data Seeding & Zero-Pollution Guardrails
| 
|   For initial app explorations, DemoDataSeeder.swift generates realistic test records: Ava Martinez with Milo
|   the Mini Goldendoodle, and Jordan Lee with Luna the Shih Tzu, complete with realistic groomer notes
|   ("Comfort breaks during drying help keep Milo relaxed", "Coat detangled well after conditioning
|   treatment"). To ensure this sample data never pollutes a real salon's books, seeding is strictly barred if
|   a single real client exists. Furthermore, when sample services are priced, SamplePriceRecord records the
|   injected price stamps in UserDefaults. If the salon later taps "Remove Sample Data", the system surgically
|   deletes only the untouched sample records, preserving any real services or custom pricing adjustments the
|   groomer made in the meantime.
|

|   ──────
|   ### Low-Level POSIX File Locking & SQLite C API Verification
|   Pawtrackr takes process synchronization down to the Unix kernel layer in StoreFileLockCoordinator.swift.
|   Before SwiftData boots, any store-family file operations (such as pre-update backups or legacy migrations)
|   acquire an advisory lock on Pawtrackr.store.lock. Rather than relying on FileManager.createFile—which
|   writes atomically by creating a new file and swapping inodes, causing separate processes to lock different
|   inodes—the coordinator invokes POSIX open(lockURL.path, O_RDWR | O_CREAT | O_CLOEXEC, 0o600) to ensure all
|   processes bind to the exact same inode. It then calls flock(descriptor, LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB) in a bounded
|   retry loop, guaranteeing that multi-instance macOS launches or background test runners never hang
|   indefinitely. Furthermore, the SQLiteStoreFileSet struct directly binds to the SQLite C API
|   (sqlite3_open_v2, sqlite3_prepare_v2) to execute PRAGMA quick_check in read-only mode (SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY
|   | SQLITE_OPEN_NOMUTEX), aborting file modifications if the database state is corrupt.
| 
|   ### The Cryptographic Snapshot Safety Boundary
|   In SecureStoreSnapshotExporter.swift, Pawtrackr contains a complete cryptographic archival subsystem
|   utilizing Apple's CryptoKit (AES.GCM) and LZFSE compression to package the entire SQLite database family
|   into an encrypted .pawtrackrbackup bundle. Crucially, this feature is intentionally hard-gated by
|   isUserFacingExportEnabled = false. The codebase explicitly documents why: physical SQLite database
|   snapshots taken while SwiftData is actively writing can result in torn WAL checkpoints, and keys stored
|   under kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly cannot be decrypted on a new device after a
|   migration. Until logical UUID-based export and insert-only merge capabilities are built, the team enforced
|   this architectural safety gate to prevent users from mistaking local physical snapshots for transferable
|   disaster backups.
| 
|   ### Sandboxed Practice Salon & Interactive Guided Academy
|   Pawtrackr features a fully isolated, interactive training simulator driven by PracticeSalon.swift and
|   WalkthroughController.swift. When a groomer or manager enters the "Academy," the app constructs an in-
|   memory ModelContainer (isStoredInMemoryOnly: true) pre-seeded with sample clients and an un-checked-in test
|   pet ("Pepper" the tabby cat). To guarantee total data isolation:
| 
|   • SpotlightIndexer is explicitly told to ignore the practice container.
|   • All temporary settings are sandboxed to a dedicated suite (com.pawtrackr.practiceSalon) that is erased on
|   exit.
|   • POS checkouts run in preview mode without saving disk drafts to CheckoutDraftStore.
|   • The walkthrough overlay dynamically tracks UI anchors across navigation transitions. It incorporates a 2-
|   second layout watchdog delay and a 15-second mission patience timer (missionPatience) that automatically
|   unlocks the "Next" button if a gesture is missed or if VoiceOver accessibility is active.
|   ### Multi-Page Vector Business Reports & Dark-Mode Proofing
|   The analytics reporting pipeline in BusinessReportFacts.swift, BusinessReportCSV.swift, and
|   BusinessReportService.swift generates audit-ready financial summaries entirely off the main thread. Rather
|   than relying on HTML rendering or web views, BusinessReportService uses CoreGraphics CGContext and a custom
|   layout engine (PDFCanvas) to draw vector Letter-sized pages. It calculates block heights dynamically,
|   enforces keepsWithNext rules to prevent orphaned section titles, and automatically splits wide tables
|   across pages with repeating header rows. The PDF renderer utilizes a fixed, calibrated print palette
|   (Palette.ink, Palette.surface, Palette.hairline) rather than system dynamic colors, preventing exported
|   PDFs from producing illegible white-on-white text when generated on a device in Dark Mode.
|   ### Materialized Analytics Caching & Change-Tracking Guards
|   To prevent dynamic SQL aggregate queries from stalling the UI as salon visit histories scale over thousands
|   of records, SummaryUpdater.swift maintains materialized aggregate entities in SwiftData: DaySummary,
|   ServiceDaySummary, CategoryDaySummary, and ClientInsightSummary. Because SwiftData marks models as dirty
|   upon any property assignment—even if the value has not changed—SummaryUpdater uses a dedicated assign(...)
|   helper that compares values before assigning, eliminating spurious database writes. During rebuilds, it
|   intentionally performs relationship prefetching (relationshipKeyPathsForPrefetching = [\.visits]) to warm
|   Core Data caches in SQLite memory and eliminate relationship fault thrashing.
| 
|   ### Background Salon Health Auditing & Churn Sentinel
|   In InsightsActor.swift, an isolated @ModelActor performs background audits of salon operational records.
|   Beyond calculating retention rates and service profitability trends, it actively screens for data
|   anomalies:
|   • Stale Active Visits: Flags visits checked in for more than 24 hours that were never checked out.
|   • Unpaid Finished Visits: Detects completed grooming sessions missing payment entries.
|   • Zero-Dollar Checkouts: Isolates comped or unpriced checkouts before they skew average ticket KPIs.
|   • Missing External References: Identifies card, Zelle, or bank transfer payments lacking reconciliation
|   references.
|   • Missing Contact Records: Finds clients without phone or email addresses to alert front-desk staff during
|   intake.
|   ### Thermal & Low-Power Aware Motion Governance
| 
|   In MotionSystem.swift, the app’s interaction and animation pipeline is regulated by MotionGovernor. The
|   governor inspects ProcessInfo.processInfo.thermalState and isLowPowerModeEnabled. If an iPad or Mac starts
|   overheating (.serious or .critical thermal state), or if battery-saver mode is active, the app dynamically
|   disables Spring animations and transitions iOS 18 3x3 MeshGradient shaders into lightweight static linear
|   gradients. Cross-platform tactile feedback in HapticManager.swift routes to the Taptic Engine on iOS
|   (UIImpactFeedbackGenerator, UINotificationFeedbackGenerator) and maps directly to Force Touch trackpad
|   impulses on macOS (NSHapticFeedbackManager).
| 
|   ### Multi-Window Concurrency Semaphore for Client Creation
| 
|   In ClientCreationCoordinator.swift, Pawtrackr solves race conditions inherent to multi-window iPad and
|   macOS environments. When multiple client intake windows or sheets open simultaneously, an async FIFO queue
|   using CheckedContinuation<Void, Never> ensures only one creation transaction proceeds at a time. The nested
|   ClientCreationWriter checks non-unique indexed keys (ClientDuplicateLookup) against both stripped phone
|   digits and Celtic/compound normalized name keys, rejecting duplicates with ClientDuplicateError before
|   persisting.

|   ### 1. Predictive Scheduling & Revenue Forecasting Engine
| 
|   The salon’s intelligence pipeline combines short-term churn prevention with long-term revenue forecasting.
|   In PredictiveForecastingEngine.swift, Pawtrackr projects up to 366 days into the future on a detached
|   .utility-priority background task. To prevent active, in-progress visits from starving the sample window of
|   actual completed revenue, its FetchDescriptor<Visit> explicitly predicates on endedAt != nil before
|   applying the 500-record query cap. It then calculates moving averages across historical daily revenue
|   buckets using pure Decimal math. Concurrently, PredictiveSchedulingActor.swift runs as a dedicated
|   @ModelActor that prefetches \.visits and \.owner. It computes an overdueRatio by measuring days past the
|   pet's recommended grooming cadence (defaulting to 30 days for dogs and 182 days / 6 months for cats, unless
|   overridden by explicit owner preference). Suggestions are ranked strictly by urgency so groomers can
|   immediately re-engage high-churn clients via pre-populated SMS deep links (smsURL), direct telephone
|   dialing (telURL), or in-app rebooking.
|   ──────
|   ### 2. Aggressive Behavior Safety Locks & Bilingual De-escalation Protocol
| 
|   In Pet.swift, staff safety is governed by a sticky handling-hazard rule. To avoid missing dangerous pets in
|   non-English locales, the safety parser folds accents and case to evaluate bilingual word stems in English
|   and Spanish ("aggressive", "agresiv", "bite", "muerde", "dangerous", "peligros"). If a pet is ever flagged
|   as aggressive, an alert banner is displayed across the client center, pet details, and active visit cards.
|   Crucially, a single quiet grooming session cannot clear the aggressive status. The method
|   reconcileBehaviorTagsFromCompletedVisits(requiredClearVisitCount: 3) enforces that an aggressive warning
|   remains active until three consecutive completed visits each contain explicit calm or cooperative tags and
|   zero bite or danger tags. Furthermore, Pet avoids SwiftData's fatal composite attribute deserialization
|   trap: enums like Species and PetGender are persisted as primitive strings (speciesRaw, genderRaw) behind
|   non-persisted @Transient properties, guaranteeing that future enum schema additions will never crash client
|   queries.
|   ──────
|   ### 3. Core Spotlight Indexer, Batch Paging & The App Lock Privacy Gate
| 
|   Device search integration in SpotlightIndexer.swift balances instant user discoverability with strict
|   customer privacy. During live editing, model setters invoke scheduleIndex, which captures thread-safe
|   snapshots and coalesces updates into a 500ms debounce queue to avoid hammering the search index on rapid
|   keystrokes. For full database re-indexing, the system iterates through Client and Pet records in batches of
|   200, creating a brand-new ModelContext for every single batch so faulted relationships, photo data, and
|   thumbnails are immediately discarded from RAM. Security is enforced through an atomic stateLock: the moment
|   App Lock (Biometrics/PIN) is enabled, or if a user triggers "Start Fresh", the indexer increments an
|   internal generation counter and issues an immediate CSSearchableIndex.default().deleteAllSearchableItems.
|   Any pending batches from older generations are dropped on the spot. In addition, the sandbox coordinator
|   registers in-memory Practice Salon containers into practiceContainers: Set<ObjectIdentifier> so test pets
|   created during interactive walkthroughs are never indexed into iOS system search.
|   ──────
|   ### 4. Cross-Platform Vector PDF Canvas & Receipt Generation
| 
|   Pawtrackr renders receipts as vector PDF documents using PDFReceiptService.swift and PDFCanvas.swift. To
|   guarantee high UI responsiveness, receipt generation is partitioned into two distinct phases: a
|   ReceiptSnapshot is assembled on the @MainActor from SwiftData models and formatted currency strings, after
|   which the vector drawing executes non-isolated on a background thread. In PDFCanvas.swift, the drawing
|   pipeline handles the discrepancy between Apple’s graphic backends: while UIKit defaults to a top-left
|   origin, AppKit on macOS draws strings into the current NSGraphicsContext using a bottom-left Cartesian
|   origin. PDFCanvas translates and flips the Mac context coordinates (context.translateBy(x: 0, y:
|   bounds.height), context.scaleBy(x: 1, y: -1)), sets NSGraphicsContext.current =
|   NSGraphicsContext(cgContext: context, flipped: true), and restores the prior graphics state upon completion
|   via defer. This guarantees that receipts rendered on macOS and iOS are byte-identical without truncated or
|   misplaced text blocks.
|   ──────
|   ### 5. Multi-Scope Search Engine & Local Hashing Vector Embeddings
|   Client lookups are handled through a dual-mode search stack. In ClientSearchQuery.swift, search queries are
|   parsed into structured AND terms supporting prefix scopes (n: for full name, f: for first name, l: for last
|   name, p: for phone, pet: for pet name, breed: for breed, and email:). Rather than reading SwiftData
|   attributes on every keystroke, searches run against an immutable, normalized in-memory struct named
|   ClientSearchRecord, while ClientStoreRevision tracks ModelContext.didSave notifications with an atomic
|   generation counter to invalidate cached entries only after real database commits. For semantic text
|   matching across clinical notes and behavior descriptions, SearchEmbeddingService.swift generates 128-
|   dimensional local vector embeddings on a detached .utility task. To remain 100% offline and eliminate
|   external network dependencies, it tokenizes alphanumeric words, applies 64-bit FNV-1a hashing
|   (14_695_981_039_346_656_037 with prime multiplier 1_099_511_628_211), assigns random projection signs
|   (((hash >> 8) & 1) == 0 ? 1 : -1), and scales vectors to L2 unit length.
|   ──────
|   ### 6. North American Numbering Plan Normalization & Emergency Dialing Rules
|   Telephone number processing in PhoneUtils.swift acts as the single source of truth for communications. It
|   maps vanity letters (e.g., FLOWERS to numeric digits), strips non-numeric characters, and validates numbers
|   against the North American Numbering Plan (NANP), rejecting special N11 service codes (such as 911, 411, or
|   211) and enforcing regex rules (^[2-9]\d{2}[2-9]\d{6}$) where area codes and exchange codes cannot start
|   with 0 or 1. Valid numbers are standardized to canonical E.164 strings (+1##########) and exposed through
|   typed URL schemes for phone calls (tel:), text messaging (sms:), and WhatsApp direct chats (wa.me/1...). To
|   prevent cursor jumping in SwiftUI forms, formatForEditing refrains from progressive reformatting until at
|   least 10 digits are typed. Companion validation in EmergencyContactRules.swift ensures that emergency
|   contacts cannot be silently dropped during client onboarding: incomplete rows require either a valid name
|   and phone or an explicit clearing action.
|   ──────
|   ### 7. App Bootstrapping, Store Health Checks & Pre-Boot Rollbacks
|   The initialization sequence in AppStoreBootstrap.swift and PawtrackrApp.swift enforces strict sequencing
|   before any persistent container is opened. If the user scheduled a database restore, the archive swap
|   executes first, creating a safety archive of the existing store. If the restored database fails to open or
|   fails the low-level SQLite integrity check in StoreHealthCheck, the system triggers
|   StoreBackupRestore.rollBackRestore(archivedDirectoryName:), immediately restoring the previous working
|   database to prevent stranding the user on a recovery screen. In unit test runs, PawtrackrApp.init detects
|   that Pawtrackr is running as the unit test host and suppresses container creation entirely, ensuring that
|   the test process owns the single active ModelContainer and preventing SwiftData object invalidation bugs.
|   On macOS, the app boots secondary window scenes including client-window, insights-window, and the live
|   menu-bar companion Pawtrackr Pulse via MenuBarExtra.
|   ──────
|   ### 8. Workload-Governed Background Maintenance & Thermal Safeguards
|   Routine system hygiene is managed by ScheduledTasks.swift, which registers background maintenance
|   (PartnerShipWithMedia.Pawtrackr.maintenance) scheduled for 3:00 AM every Sunday. Before executing resource-
|   intensive operations—specifically SummaryUpdater.rebuildAllSummaries and image pruning via
|   DataPruner.pruneOldPhotos—it evaluates SystemWorkloadPolicy.swift. If iOS Low Power Mode is active or the
|   device's thermal state reaches .serious or .critical, background maintenance is automatically deferred. In
|   addition, ScheduledTasks checks for simulator runtimes to prevent submitting unsupported
|   BGProcessingTaskRequest calls that would otherwise log false positive errors during local development.
|   ──────
|   ### 9. Keychain-Hardened PIN Lockout & App Switcher Privacy Blur
|   Brute-force security is decoupled from ephemeral view state in PinLockoutGuard.swift. Rather than storing
|   failed attempt counters in SwiftUI @State (which an attacker could reset by simply force-quitting the app),
|   all failure counters and lockout deadlines are written directly to the iOS Keychain via KeychainStorage.
|   Because Keychain items survive app restarts, force-quits, and complete app reinstallations, the security
|   throttle cannot be bypassed without a server. The lockout follows an escalating cooldown ladder: attempts 1
|   through 4 are free, the 5th failure initiates a 1-minute lockout, the 6th increases to 2 minutes, the 7th
|   to 5 minutes, and 8 or more failures cap at a 15-minute penalty. For visual privacy,
|   PrivacyScreenScenePolicy detects whenever the app transitions to .inactive or .background (such as opening
|   the iOS App Switcher) and overlays PrivacyScreen using .ultraThinMaterial, blocking sensitive client phone
|   numbers, addresses, and daily revenue numbers from being captured in system task switcher screenshots.
|   ──────
|   ### 10. StoreKit 2 Pro Monopolization & Timeout-Protected Paywall
|   Monetization for Pawtrackr Pro in EntitlementStore.swift adheres strictly to ADR-0001 and ADR-0003:
|   StoreKit 2 is the sole source of truth, and no SwiftData @Model is ever created for entitlements. The store
|   maintains an active listener across the app's lifetime on Transaction.updates to react immediately to
|   renewals, family sharing, revocations, and refunds. Because Apple does not emit transaction updates when a
|   cancelled subscription naturally expires at the end of a billing period, EntitlementStore runs
|   armExpiryRefresh(), scheduling a targeted sleep task to re-verify Transaction.currentEntitlements exactly
|   two seconds after the known expiration date. Furthermore, product lookups are wrapped inside
|   StoreKitTimeout.run(seconds: 2.0), ensuring that throttled or offline network requests never trap the
|   paywall in an infinite spinner, while product.purchase() remains unbounded so users can take their time
|   authorizing with Face ID or Apple Pay.
|   ──────
|   ### 11. Centralized Wall-Clock Time Hub & Visit Timer Synchronization
| 
|   Active grooming sessions display live elapsed times using VisitTimer.swift without causing timer jitter or
|   excessive CPU wakeups. Instead of having dozens of individual visit rows run independent Combine timers,
|   all active timers subscribe to TimeHub.swift. TimeHub maintains a single DispatchSourceTimer running on
|   DispatchQueue.main. It calculates the offset to the upcoming integer second (ceil(nowRef) - nowRef) so its
|   ticks align precisely with the system clock, incorporating a 200ms leeway for battery optimization.
|   VisitTimer calculates its elapsed seconds from absolute dates (startedAt and now), ensuring that visit
|   timers survive backgrounding, phone sleep, and device orientation changes without losing count. When
|   VoiceOver is enabled, accessibilityElapsedLabel produces spelled-out duration strings (e.g., "1 hour 12
|   minutes") using a localized DateComponentsFormatter.
|   ──────
|   ### 12. Multi-Window Concurrent Edit Reconciler & Conflict Resolver
| 
|   In a multi-window macOS or iPadOS environment, concurrent client editing is protected by
|   ClientEditConflict.swift. When an edit sheet or inline detail header opens, it records a ClientEditBaseline
|   containing the record's clientUUID, updatedAt, lastModifiedBy, and contact fields. When the groomer taps
|   Save, the engine checks whether the record in the store has been updated by another window or device
|   (hasChangeFromAnotherDevice). If conflicting changes are detected, it halts the save and yields
|   .changedElsewhere rather than silently overwriting the other user's input. When saving succeeds,
|   changedFields calculates a minimal diff and applies only the specific attributes modified by the user (such
|   as updating an address while leaving concurrent updates to loyalty points, pet records, or notes intact)
|   through a fresh background ModelContext.

|   ### CoreBluetooth Thermal Hardware Driver & The ESC/POS Protocol
| 
|   Pawtrackr bridges native iPadOS and macOS POS checkout workflows directly to physical retail counter
|   hardware via BluetoothPeripheralManager.swift. Because retail salon printers (such as Munbyn, Star
|   Micronics, Epson, and generic Bluetooth 4.0/5.0 receipt printers) use vendor-specific profiles rather than
|   AirPrint, the manager operates a custom CoreBluetooth central pipeline equipped with the permanent
|   restoration identifier "PartnerShipWithMedia.Pawtrackr.bluetooth.central". When iOS suspends or terminates
|   the app in the background, state restoration in centralManager(_:willRestoreState:) automatically rebinds
|   discovered peripherals, filtering restored devices by descriptor hints so that a connected cash drawer or
|   RFID scanner is never mistakenly adopted as the thermal receipt printer.
|   Receipts are generated through the pure-binary ESC/POS builder ThermalReceiptPayloadBuilder. The builder
|   formats receipts into a strict 42-column fixed-width layout, normalizing em-dashes and typographic ellipses
|   into ASCII bytes. Raw byte sequences initialize the print head ([0x1B, 0x40]), toggle center alignment
|   ([0x1B, 0x61, 0x01]) and bold emphasis ([0x1B, 0x45, 0x01]), pulse the RJ11/RJ12 solenoid to trigger
|   physical cash drawers upon cash checkout completion ([0x1B, 0x70, 0x00, 0x19, 0xFA]), and execute an
|   automated partial paper cut ([0x1D, 0x56, 0x41, 0x10]). To prevent buffer overflows and dropped packets on
|   low-energy thermal printers, write(payload:timeout:) chunks transmission dynamically to the peripheral's
|   maximumWriteValueLength(for:). When writing without response, it polls canSendWriteWithoutResponse with
|   micro-sleep intervals, guaranteeing that lengthy itemized grooming receipts transmit smoothly without
|   blocking the SwiftUI main thread.
|   ──────
|   ### Non-Destructive Store Backups, SQLite Journaling & Recovery Architecture
|   To protect user data from migration regressions, Pawtrackr implements a multi-tiered file rotation and
|   recovery engine in StoreBackupRestore.swift and StoreFileMigration.swift. The engine categorizes store
|   snapshots into four distinct directory namespaces:
| 
|   1. RecoveryBackup-<timestamp> (snapshots created when a user initiates a data reset from the recovery
|   screen),
|   2. PreMigrationBackup-<build>-<timestamp> (automatic snapshots created before the app boots a new build
|   version),
|   3. StoreMigrationBackup-<timestamp> (archives created if an empty named store replaces a legacy unnamed
|   store), and
|   4. PreRestoreBackup-<timestamp> (safety copies of the live store taken immediately before restoring a
|   historical snapshot).
| 
|   Crucially, no operation ever deletes a database file. When a restore is executed in
|   StoreBackupRestore.performScheduledRestoreIfNeeded, the active store family (Pawtrackr.store, -wal, and -
|   shm) is moved atomically into PreRestoreBackup-, external photo blobs stored in .Pawtrackr_SUPPORT are
|   merged via mergeMissingFiles without overwriting newer assets, and an explanatory README.txt manifest is
|   generated. If the restored store fails container validation on boot, rollBackRestore immediately swaps the
|   archived original back into place.
|   To evaluate backup contents without triggering SwiftData schemas or initializing Core Data stacks,
|   StoreFileMigration.clientRowCount and clientUUIDs query the SQLite database directly using low-level C APIs
|   (sqlite3_open_v2 with SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY). If a lone .store file lacks its corresponding -shm shared
|   memory file, the reader falls back to SQLite's immutable=1 URI flag to read table counts without failure.
|   When candidate stores contain clients missing from the current active database (excluding sample practice
|   clients), publishOffer publishes a non-intrusive restore banner on the dashboard. In-flight file moves are
|   coordinated under POSIX locks (StoreFileLockCoordinator) and tracked using StoreMigrationJournal, allowing
|   interrupted file operations to self-heal on the subsequent launch.
|   ──────
|   ### Loyalty Points Engine & Unlinked Audit Ledger
|   Client retention and rewards are governed by LoyaltyEngine.swift and LoyaltyService.swift. All calculations
|   are pure, synchronous, and integer-deterministic, ensuring that preview simulations in the UI and actual
|   checkout transactions calculate identical point awards. The engine supports two earning modes:
|   pointsPerDollar (which multiplies money totals rounded to 4 decimal places before integer conversion) and
|   flatPerVisit. On top of the base points, tier multipliers (Bronze 100%, Silver 110%, Gold 125%, Platinum
|   150%) are applied using floor integer arithmetic (base * multiplier / 100). Clients who rebook a return
|   appointment within the 45-day window (rebookWindowDays = 45) earn a flat 20-point bonus
|   (rebookBonusPoints = 20).
|   To record point mutations without risking data corruption, all balance changes are audited via
|   LoyaltyLedgerEntry.swift. Following the same crash-proof design as CheckoutTransaction, ledger entries link
|   to clientUUID and visitUUID solely through primitive UUID properties rather than SwiftData relationship
|   graphs. This prevents cascade-deletion bugs: if a client or visit is subsequently archived or deleted, the
|   financial and loyalty audit ledger remains intact. Furthermore, in LoyaltyCheckoutProcessor.applyEarnings,
|   when an existing checkout is re-opened or adjusted, the processor delta-updates the client's balance
|   (client.loyaltyPoints += points - previousPoints) and mutates the existing .earned ledger entry in-place
|   rather than appending duplicate rows.
|   ──────
|   ### Onboarding State Machine & Re-Render Loop Defense
| 
|   Initial app setup is managed by OnboardingViewModel.swift. The view model coordinates an 8-step onboarding
|   wizard covering business profile configuration, regional currency, staff roles, and PIN creation. During
|   development, SwiftUI view recreation exposed a critical loop: evaluating @State initializers during parent
|   re-renders caused premature writes to @AppStorage, which triggered invalidations and froze the app on a
|   blank screen. To eliminate this, OnboardingViewModel introduces an isInitializing gate that blocks draft
|   disk synchronization until user input occurs.
| 
|   Security boundaries are strictly enforced: while draft form fields (business name, address, contact
|   numbers) are persisted to temporary preferences so users can resume setup after switching apps, the
|   security PIN and confirmation fields live exclusively in memory (OnboardingViewModel.pin). PINs are never
|   serialized to draft plists, and are committed directly to the iOS Keychain via AppSettings.changePIN upon
|   final completion. When the user completes onboarding, a detached background task in
|   finish(seedSampleData:onComplete:) validates sample data seed policies (SampleDataSeedPolicy), seeds the
|   default grooming service catalog (DataMigrations.ensureServiceCatalog), installs bilingual client
|   communication templates, and primes the interactive feature tour.
|   ──────
|   ### The Academy Sandbox: Practice Salon & Side-Effect Firewall
|   Pawtrackr features an interactive training academy powered by PracticeSalon.swift. Instead of running
|   training guides over production client records, the app constructs an isolated in-memory sandbox:
|     let configuration = ModelConfiguration(
|         "PracticeSalon-\(UUID().uuidString)",
|         schema: schema,
|         isStoredInMemoryOnly: true,
|         cloudKitDatabase: .none
|     )
| 
|   This ephemeral container is populated with realistic demo clients (including Ava and her waiting cat
|   Pepper, injected specifically for check-in tutorials) and discarded entirely when the session concludes or
|   the app terminates.
|   To keep the sandbox strictly quarantined from the real salon, a four-layer side-effect firewall is
|   enforced:
|   1. Spotlight Isolation: The sandbox container registers with
|   SpotlightIndexer.shared.beginPracticeSalon(container), suppressing indexing so demo clients never appear in
|   iOS search results.
|   2. UserDefaults Isolation: Pricing experiments and practice overrides are routed to a private suite ("com.
|   pawtrackr.practiceSalon"), which is purged upon closing.
|   3. Handoff & Checklist Suppression: Views inspect EnvironmentValues.isPracticeSalon, preventing demo visits
|   from broadcasting Continuity activities or falsely completing business setup checklists.
|   4. Checkout Draft Shield: POS checkouts performed inside the tour bypass CheckoutDraftStore, preventing
|   recovery files from being written to disk.
|   ──────
|   ### Background Analytics, Anomaly Auditing & Thermal Motion Governance
| 
|   Heavy reporting and trend computations run on a dedicated background actor in InsightsActor.swift. Rather
|   than running dynamic table scans across thousands of historical visits on the UI thread, metrics are
|   computed from materialized daily views (DaySummary, ServiceDaySummary, and CategoryDaySummary) maintained
|   by SummaryUpdater.swift. The actor aggregates revenue distributions, payment method breakdowns, and 6-month
|   trailing growth buckets before handing ready-to-render view models to InsightsView.swift. Full analytical
|   reports can be exported to spreadsheet format using BusinessReportCSV.swift, which compiles period
|   comparisons, service shares, and top-spender summaries.
| 
|   Beyond standard metrics, fetchDataQualityIssues runs continuous data integrity audits:
| 
|   • Stale Active Visits: Flags any visit remaining checked in for over 24 hours without an end time
|   (preventing salon workload skew).
|   • Missing Payments: Highlights completed visits that lack a corresponding Payment entity.
|   • Zero-Dollar Checkouts: Identifies comped or unpriced checkouts that require managerial review.
|   • Missing Card/Zelle References: Detects electronic transactions lacking authorization or confirmation
|   codes required for deposit reconciliation.
|   • Missing Client Contact: Surfaces customer profiles with neither phone nor email, preventing recall
|   campaign failures.
| 
|   Finally, visual effects and haptic responses are throttled dynamically by MotionGovernor.swift and
|   HapticManager.swift. In MotionGovernor.shouldAnimate, animated mesh gradients (InsightsMeshBackground) and
|   continuous spring effects are evaluated against system state: if the user enables
|   accessibilityReduceMotion, if Low Power Mode is active, or if device thermals enter .serious or .critical,
|   complex shaders drop back to static LinearGradients to protect battery health and prevent frame drops.
|   Tactile feedback is similarly optimized: on iOS, HapticManager fires Taptic Engine feedback generators
|   (UIImpactFeedbackGenerator), while on macOS it seamlessly maps feedback to Force Touch Trackpads via
|   NSHapticFeedbackManager.defaultPerformer.        I'm consolidating all visit stopwatches into a single synchronized clock hub, ensuring precise timing acro...
|   ### The Core Identity and Philosophy of Pawtrackr
|   Pawtrackr is an offline-first Point-of-Sale (POS), Customer Relationship Management (CRM), and grooming
|   management workstation built for modern pet salons. Its purpose is to deliver zero-latency operations at
|   the physical service counter, completely decoupling the salon's daily survival from internet connectivity,
|   cloud outages, or remote database synchronization failures.
|   To achieve this without compromising data integrity, every layer of Pawtrackr operates under strict
|   architectural guardrails: financial transactions utilize exact Decimal arithmetic (no floating-point
|   rounding errors), database mutations avoid destructive migrations, hardware communication runs natively
|   over CoreBluetooth ESC/POS protocols, and all customer data remains on device under direct salon ownership.
|   ──────
|   ### Derived Aggregate Maintenance and Relationship Warming (SummaryUpdater.swift)
|   To keep dashboards, revenue graphs, and business reports responsive without constantly querying hundreds of
|   raw visit records, Pawtrackr maintains four derived aggregate models: DaySummary, ServiceDaySummary,
|   CategoryDaySummary, and ClientInsightSummary. Because the app deliberately omits @Attribute(.unique) from
|   its SwiftData schema (a decision made in ADR-0004 to eliminate migration crashes), multiple aggregate rows
|   for a single calendar day can exist following concurrent inserts or database restores. SummaryUpdater.swift
|   resolves this through deterministic deduplication: when comparing duplicate day summaries, isPreferred
|   prioritizes the entry with the higher completed visitCount, followed by the higher total revenue.
|   During full rebuilds (rebuildAllSummaries), SummaryUpdater prevents SQLite N + 1 query cascades by
|   configuring descriptor.relationshipKeyPathsForPrefetching = [\Visit.items, \Visit.pet]. Furthermore, it
|   executes a preemptive prefetch of \Pet.visits across all pets so that the per-client lifetime spending loop
|   does not fault relationships one row at a time. To protect the main thread and avoid false view re-renders,
|   the update engine uses an assign helper that checks equality before writing back to the model: SwiftData
|   flags models as dirty whenever a property is assigned even if the value is unchanged, so this check
|   prevents redundant context saves and spurious SwiftUI view tree updates.
|   ──────
|   ### Non-Reentrant Client Creation Coordination (ClientCreationCoordinator.swift, ClientRepository.swift)
|   Without unique database constraints, rapid duplicate taps or multi-window forms could insert duplicate
|   client records. ClientCreationCoordinator.swift solves this by managing a FIFO ticket queue using
|   CheckedContinuation<Void, Never>. Only one client creation process may execute at any given instant across
|   all app windows and sheets. Before opening the write gate, prepareSearchKeys scans older databases in
|   bounded chunks of 200 records to backfill missing indexed search keys off the main actor.
|   Within the atomic creation block, ClientDuplicateLookup runs a two-tier match check: it first searches for
|   exact digit-only phone matches via PhoneUtils.searchKey, falling back to normalized full-name strings. If
|   no duplicate exists, the client, their pets (with generated thumbnails and behavior flags), emergency
|   contacts, and a localized creation notification are inserted atomically into the ModelContext. Immediately
|   following context persistence, the new entity is scheduled with SpotlightIndexer.shared.scheduleIndex so
|   that iOS Spotlight indexing can locate the pet by name or the owner by normalized phone number. On client
|   deletion (deleteClient), the repository deletes the entity, purges Spotlight index entries, and identifies
|   every calendar day where that client had a visit or payment to trigger a focused SummaryUpdater.rebuildDay,
|   keeping salon revenue totals accurate.
|   ──────
|   ### Field-Level Multi-Context Edit Conflict Protection (ClientEditConflict.swift)
|   Salon operators often view and edit client contact details while another device or background worker
|   completes an active visit or adds loyalty points. If an edit form saved the entire client model blindly, it
|   would overwrite those changes with stale data. ClientEditConflict.swift isolates edited fields into
|   ClientContactFields (firstName, lastName, phone, email, address) in view @State.
|   When the user taps Save, ClientEditSaver re-reads the client from SQLite via an independent ModelContext
|   and evaluates hasChangeFromAnotherDevice. Critically, a simple change in updatedAt is not treated as a
|   conflict: adding a pet, completing a grooming visit, or earning loyalty rewards updates the client's
|   timestamp without changing contact fields. A conflict is raised only if the timestamp changed, the
|   modifying device ID differs from DeviceIdentity.currentID, and the contact fields themselves differ.
|   Furthermore, ClientEditSaver performs diff-based patching: it modifies only the specific contact fields
|   altered in that form session. If a groomer updates a phone number while another updates an address, neither
|   change is overwritten.
|   ──────
|   ### StoreKit 2 Monolithic Entitlements and Expiration Boundaries (EntitlementStore.swift,                  
|   SubscriptionPaywallView.swift)
| 
|   Pawtrackr’s subscription engine strictly adheres to ADR-0001 and ADR-0003: StoreKit 2 is the sole source of
|   truth. There is no persisted SwiftData model for subscription status, eliminating schema migrations when
|   subscription structures change. Subscription trials are powered natively by Apple's introductory offers
|   (offer?.type == .introductory), preventing client-side clock tampering. EntitlementStore runs a persistent
|   background listener over Transaction.updates throughout the application lifecycle to process renewals,
|   cancellations, and family-shared grants immediately.
|   A subtle StoreKit edge case is handled in armExpiryRefresh: Apple emits no transaction update notification
|   when a cancelled subscription naturally expires at the end of its billing cycle. Without intervention, an
|   app would remain unlocked indefinitely. EntitlementStore solves this by calculating delay =
|   expiration.timeIntervalSinceNow + 2 and arming a sleeping background task that automatically re-evaluates
|   Transaction.currentEntitlements right after the expiration cutoff. To defend against unresponsive network
|   states during paywall loading, StoreKitTimeout races Product.products(for:) calls against a strict 2.0-
|   second wall-clock deadline in a throwing task group, surfacing an actionable retry button rather than an
|   endless loading indicator.
|   ──────
|   ### Synchronized Timing and Thermal-Aware Motion Governance (VisitTimer.swift, MotionSystem.swift,         
|   HapticManager.swift)
|   In a busy salon with multiple pets in grooming stations simultaneously, independent timers per active visit
|   row would trigger uncoordinated view re-renders and drain device battery. VisitTimer.swift connects all
|   stopwatches to a shared clock hub (TimeHub.shared.$now), ensuring that every timer tick fires on the exact
|   same millisecond boundary. When the scene resigns active state, ticking is cancelled to conserve power;
|   when resumed, elapsed time is recomputed from absolute dates (Calendar.current.dateComponents([.second],
|   from: started, to: now)), preserving accuracy even after hours of background suspension. Spelled-out labels
|   are generated using DateComponentsFormatter (.unitsStyle = .full) so that VoiceOver announces "1 hour 15
|   minutes" instead of fragmented abbreviations.
| 
|   Visual effects and tactile feedback are governed by environmental and physical conditions. MotionGovernor
|   checks accessibilityReduceMotion, ProcessInfo.processInfo.isLowPowerModeEnabled, and device thermal state:
|   if ProcessInfo.processInfo.thermalState reaches .serious or .critical, dynamic 3x3 SIMD2-based MeshGradient
|   calculations and spring physics are dropped, falling back to static linear gradients to keep the hardware
|   cool during high-volume workdays. Tactile feedback in HapticManager.swift provides native haptic feedback
|   on iOS via UIImpactFeedbackGenerator and on macOS via NSHapticFeedbackManager.defaultPerformer for Force
|   Touch trackpads, toggled dynamically via user preferences.
|   ──────
|   ### The Academy Onboarding System and Sample Sandbox (WalkthroughController.swift, SampleData.swift,       
|   PracticeSalon.swift)
| 
|   To train salon staff without risking live production records, Pawtrackr incorporates an interactive Academy
|   engine (WalkthroughController.swift). Structured across five chapters (WalkthroughLesson: Dashboard, Client
|   Directory, Profiles & Pets, Visits & Payments, and Insights & Backups), the walkthrough coordinates element
|   spotlights using live geometric anchors (.walkthroughAnchor) or platform-specific fallbacks
|   (SpotlightFallback). Stops require real interaction—such as typing "Milo" into search, tapping a filter
|   pill, or opening the checkout sheet. A 2-second target watchdog (targetWatchdogDelay) and a 15-second
|   mission patience timer (missionPatience) ensure that if an element fails to appear or a user hesitates, the
|   step unlocks "Next" or transitions the bubble to the root overlay so the flow never locks up.
| 
|   The sandbox is kept safe through deterministic UUID isolation in SampleData.swift. Sample clients, pets,
|   and visits carry fixed UUIDs (such as 5A3D1E00-0000-4000-8000-00000000C001 for Ava and ...D001 for Milo).
|   Because sample identification never relies on name strings, a real client named "Ava Martinez" with a pet
|   named "Milo" can never be misidentified as sample data. If real clients exist in the database,
|   WalkthroughTourContext.isExplainOnly switches all walkthrough steps into look-only mode: all buttons that
|   would check in a pet, save a client, or process a payment advance the tour instead of modifying the live
|   store, keeping real salon records untouched.

|   Pawtrackr's architecture demonstrates meticulous engineering across every layer—spanning low-level SQLite
|   store orchestration, process-safe file locking, CoreGraphics vector document synthesis, and operating-
|   system-level privacy boundaries.
|   Below is an exhaustive synthesis of the mechanisms, edge cases, and subsystem designs that govern the app.
|   ──────
|   ### 1. Spotlight Privacy Governance & Cross-Process Isolation
|   Customer privacy and data containment are enforced at the OS boundary in SpotlightIndexer.swift and
|   SpotlightContent.swift. When a salon enables App Lock in AppSettings.swift:224-245, Pawtrackr treats the
|   device's system search index as an untrusted surface. Because iOS Spotlight searches are accessible from
|   the lock screen or by unauthorized individuals holding the salon's iPad, Pawtrackr mandates that having an
|   active PIN immediately purges all indexed records via CSSearchableIndex.default().deleteAllSearchableItems.
|   The policy evaluation and submission happen under an internal NSLock (stateLock) with an atomic generation
|   counter. If App Lock engages while a background reindexing task is running, the generation increments,
|   instantly invalidating inflight batch jobs before they can publish customer PII to the operating system.
|   Inverted deep linking and practice sandbox isolation are deeply integrated into Spotlight. Deep links use
|   custom URL schemes parsed by SpotlightIdentifier (pawtrackr://client/<UUID> and pawtrackr://pet/<UUID>),
|   which route directly through onContinueUserActivity(CSSearchableItemActionType) in
|   PawtrackrApp.swift:266-305. To prevent test clients from leaking into system search,
|   SpotlightIndexer.beginPracticeSalon registers in-memory walkthrough containers (practiceContainers:
|   Set<ObjectIdentifier>). Setters check isPracticeRecord(in:) to ensure Academy clients never touch
|   CSSearchableIndex. Furthermore, live customer edits avoid SQLite thread starvation by copying immutable
|   snapshots (SpotlightClientSnapshot) on the caller’s context thread, coalescing multiple field changes into
|   a 500ms debouncing buffer on a dedicated serial utility queue.
|   ──────
|   ### 2. POSIX Store Locking & Pre-Boot Store-Family Migration
|   Database lifecycle management executes strictly outside the SwiftData runtime. In
|   StoreFileLockCoordinator.swift, file-level operations are synchronized across multiple processes and
|   threads using POSIX flock on Pawtrackr.store.lock. Rather than using FileManager.createFile (which swaps
|   file inodes on every write and breaks mutual exclusion between concurrent processes), the coordinator opens
|   the descriptor using open(lockURL.path, O_RDWR | O_CREAT | O_CLOEXEC, 0o600). To prevent deadlocks when an
|   internal task makes re-entrant calls, an NSRecursiveLock tracks heldLockDepth per thread. All acquisitions
|   enforce a bounded 3-second timeout (defaultTimeout) with non-blocking polls (LOCK_NB / usleep), ensuring
|   that secondary Mac instances or background worker threads cannot stall launch.
|   Store upgrades and backup safety run in PawtrackrApp.init via StoreFileMigration.swift before any
|   ModelContainer opens. When StoreFileMigration.backupStoresForCurrentBuildIfNeeded detects a new
|   CFBundleVersion, it copies the entire SQLite family (.store, .store-wal, .store-shm) and the
|   .Pawtrackr_SUPPORT/ directory (housing @Attribute(.externalStorage) pet photos and logos) into an immutable
|   snapshot directory named PreMigrationBackup-<build>-<timestamp>. Crucially, StoreFileMigration bypasses
|   SwiftData entirely to verify store contents, querying the raw SQLite C API against operational tables
|   (ZCLIENT, ZPET, ZVISIT, ZPAYMENT, ZVISITITEM, ZCHECKOUTTRANSACTION, ZINVENTORYITEM, ZINVENTORYTRANSACTION,
|   ZLOYALTYLEDGERENTRY). If an update creates an empty Pawtrackr.store while a legacy default.store with data
|   sits alongside it, the engine detects this condition and restores the legacy database over the empty shell.
|   ──────
|   ### 3. Non-Destructive Recovery Architecture & The Snapshot Boundary
|   Pawtrackr strictly adheres to an architectural mandate: nothing deletes a store. In
|   StoreBackupRestore.swift and DataStoreRecoveryView.swift, if a ModelContainer fails to initialize, the user
|   is never guided toward destructive deletion. Instead, the UI reads the low-level SQLite client count
|   directly and displays a reassurance banner: "X clients are saved on this device." If a recovery reset is
|   triggered, the existing database files are rotated into RecoveryBackup-<stamp>/. On the next app launch,
|   StoreBackupRestore.applyScheduledRestoreIfNeeded swaps files while the process is offline, moving the
|   active container into PreRestoreBackup-<stamp>/ so that every recovery operation remains completely
|   reversible.
|   The rationale behind disabling user-facing snapshot exports in SecureStoreSnapshotExporter.swift
|   exemplifies defensive system design. Although an AES-GCM encrypted container pipeline was implemented using
|   CryptoKit and LZFSE compression, it remains locked under isUserFacingExportEnabled = false. The engine's
|   inline architecture documentation explicitly notes that backing up raw SQLite files while the application
|   is actively writing in WAL mode risks torn checkpoints between the primary database and WAL index.
|   Furthermore, saving keys under kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly prevents package restoration
|   across different devices or after an iCloud device migration. Consequently, Pawtrackr forbids raw encrypted
|   store dumps in favor of deterministic CSV exports and pre-boot folder rotations.
|   ──────
|   ### 4. Bounded Nanp Normalization & Text Input Stabilization
|   Phone number handling and SMS integration are centralized in PhoneUtils.swift, which enforces North
|   American Numbering Plan (NANP) specifications:
|   • Vanity Translation & Digit Stripping: Maps characters (A–Z) to dial pad digits via vanityMap and strips
|   non-numeric characters.
|   • NANP & N11 Validation: Rejects service codes (211, 311, 411, 511, 611, 711, 811, 911) in both the area
|   code and central office exchange ([2-9]XX [2-9]XX XXXX).
|   • Cursor Stability in SwiftUI: Solves cursor-jumping regressions in PhoneUtils.formatForEditing. Formatting
|   text on every keystroke in SwiftUI causes the cursor to reset to the end of the text field. Pawtrackr
|   leaves partial entries unformatted until the input reaches a valid 10- or 11-digit boundary, allowing
|   smooth typing and paste operations.
|   • Cross-Platform Communication Schemes: Constructs E.164 strings (+1##########) for tel: and sms: URLs, and
|   generates international WhatsApp web links (https://wa.me/1##########?text=...). In
|   CommunicationSheet.swift:151-171, URLs dispatch conditionally via UIApplication.shared.open on iOS or
|   NSWorkspace.shared.open on macOS.
|   ──────
|   ### 5. Multi-Period Business Reporting & CoreGraphics Vector Pagination
|   Salon intelligence is driven by BusinessReportFacts.swift, BusinessReportCSV.swift, and
|   BusinessReportService.swift. Rather than triggering multiple unindexed queries, BusinessReportFacts.build
|   executes a single query for finished visits over the requested period plus a prior comparison period and a
|   trailing six-month window (min(previousStart, firstMonth) to periodEnd). The calculation engine performs
|   all financial aggregations in Decimal via .roundedMoney():
|   • Comparative Metrics: Period revenue vs. prior period revenue, ticket volume, average visit value, and
|   active client retention (distinguishing new clients from returning clients).
|   • Service & Payment Lines: Top revenue drivers, payment method breakdowns, top 5 client spend leaderboards,
|   and busiest day of the week (with deterministic tie-breaking preferring earlier calendar weekdays).
|   • Executive PDF Rendering: BusinessReportService generates US Letter PDF documents using raw CoreGraphics.
|   It draws KPI stat tiles, sparkline revenue trend charts, and structured data tables with relative column
|   widths and inline share-percentage bars. Tables that exceed page bounds automatically break across pages
|   while repeating their header rows and appending standard "Page X of Y" footers. To ensure clean export in
|   all environments, it uses fixed print-safe color palettes, preventing Dark Mode system styles from
|   rendering unreadable white-on-white text.
|   • Spreadsheet Ingestion: BusinessReportCSV outputs formatted CSVs prepended with a UTF-8 Byte Order Mark
|   (0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF), ensuring Microsoft Excel displays accented client and pet names properly without
|   character corruption.
