|  ### Advanced Offline Search Architecture & Snapshot Thread-Decoupling
| 
|   Pawtrackr implements a completely self-contained semantic and full-text search engine without relying on
|   external ML runtimes, cloud embeddings, or device-level CoreML model dependencies. In
|   SearchEmbeddingService.swift, standard Swift hashing (hashValue) is avoided because Apple’s runtime seeds
|   SipHash-1-3 per process launch, which would invalidate and corrupt cached indices across application
|   restarts. Instead, the engine implements a deterministic 64-bit FNV-1a hash algorithm (offset:
|   14_695_981_039_346_656_037, prime: 1_099_511_628_211) mapped across a 128-dimensional unit vector. To
|   minimize bucket collisions across small string tokens, it uses a sign-bit extraction trick ((hash >> 8) & 1
|   == 0 ? 1 : -1) to distribute negative and positive weights before applying Euclidean L2 normalization
|   (sqrt(sumOfSquares)).
|   At the query layer in ClientSearchQuery.swift, live UI keystrokes never query or fault SwiftData context
|   models directly, which would cause severe main-thread stutters when searching thousands of records.
|   Instead, queries run against an in-memory collection of lightweight, immutable ClientSearchRecord value
|   structs. Revision caching is governed by ClientStoreRevision.shared, which observes ModelContext.didSave to
|   update a 64-bit generation counter. Keystrokes support rich domain prefixes—such as n: for full name, f:
|   for first name, l: for last name, p: or phone: for contiguous phone digits, pet: for pet name, breed:, and
|   email:—with phone numbers stripped of punctuation down to digits so groomers can type partial strings like
|   "55512" and instantly match "(555) 123-4567".
|   ──────
|   ### Predictive Scheduling, Cadence Normalization, and Revenue Forecasting
| 
|   In PredictiveSchedulingActor.swift, pet rebooking reminders are not driven by raw calendar days elapsed,
|   because a 6-week gap is normal for a Doodle or Bichon Frise but represents extreme churn risk for a high-
|   frequency bath dog or a show coat. The engine calculates an overdue ratio:
| 
|                    timeSinceLastVisit
|     overdueRatio = ──────────────────
|                     expectedInterval
| 
|   where species and breed baselines establish default cadences (dogs ~4–6 weeks, cats ~6 months). A cat
|   overdue by 3 weeks produces a low urgency score, whereas a matting-prone dog overdue by 3 weeks triggers a
|   .critical rating. Based on the calculated ratio, the actor automatically prescribes prioritized outreach
|   actions: .rebook if within the regular window, .text for mild delays, and .call for severe churn risk.
|   For business intelligence, PredictiveForecastingEngine.swift computes rolling revenue forecasts using a 14-
|   day simple moving average (SMA) with a minimum 10-day historical data threshold. The engine filters
|   completed visits before applying window limits to prevent partial or in-progress checkouts from
|   artificially depressing projected ticket averages. It enforces strict boundary clamping—capping forecast
|   horizons to a maximum of 366 days and discarding negative intervals—ensuring analytics never output
|   unphysical growth curves even during extended salon holiday shutdowns.
|   ──────
|   ### Cross-Platform Graphics Normalization & Thermal POS Slips
|   Generating identical PDF receipts across iOS and macOS requires bridging divergent CoreGraphics coordinate
|   systems. In PDFCanvas.swift and PDFReceiptService.swift, text rendering via AppKit
|   (NSString.draw(at:withAttributes:)) fails silently inside CoreGraphics PDF contexts unless
|   NSGraphicsContext.current is explicitly bound to the PDF's CGContext. Furthermore, macOS PDF contexts
|   require a coordinate matrix inversion:
|     context.translateBy(x: 0, y: bounds.height)
|     context.scaleBy(x: 1.0, y: -1.0)
|   The PDF rendering pipeline creates paginated US Letter invoices and 80mm thermal slip documents that
|   dynamically compute layout heights, text word-wrapping, custom salon vector letterheads, tax breakdowns,
|   gratuity lines, and client loyalty point totals.
| 
|   For physical counter printers, BluetoothPeripheralManager.swift bypasses PDF rasterization entirely,
|   generating raw ESC/POS byte sequences. It formats invoices with double-width headers (GS ! 0x11), bold item
|   names (ESC E 1), right-aligned currency strings, and automated paper cut commands (GS V 66 0), followed by
|   pulse pins (ESC p 0 25 250) to trigger physical cash drawers upon completed cash checkouts. Real-device
|   discovery is guarded so that iOS Simulators gracefully skip Bluetooth hardware discovery without polluting
|   OSLog with unfixable CoreBluetooth errors.
|   ──────
|   ### Background Maintenance, Device Workload Throttling, and Non-Destructive Storage
|   Autonomous database grooming is coordinated by ScheduledTasks.swift using Apple's BGProcessingTaskScheduler
|   registered under the identifier "PartnerShipWithMedia.Pawtrackr.maintenance". Maintenance is scheduled
|   weekly for Sunday at 3:00 AM (weekday: 1, hour: 3, minute: 0, second: 0). If the device is powered off or
|   in low-power state during that window, a launch fallback (runMaintenance(reason: "launch fallback"))
|   triggers upon the next app startup. Crucially, background submissions are bypassed on the iOS Simulator
|   (#if targetEnvironment(simulator)), eliminating continuous .unavailable submission failure warnings during
|   development.
| 
|   Maintenance tasks operate under SystemWorkloadPolicy.swift. If
|   ProcessInfo.processInfo.isLowPowerModeEnabled is active or thermal states escalate to .serious or
|   .critical, background maintenance immediately defers execution. When running,
|   SummaryUpdater.rebuildAllSummaries(in:) recalculates daily financial rollups. For media storage,
|   DataPruner.swift treats client grooming photos as permanent historical portfolio data rather than
|   disposable cache: photo deletion is disabled by default (pruneStoredPhotos = false). If photo downsampling
|   is explicitly commanded, it processes visits in 100-record batches, downsampling multi-megabyte high-
|   resolution before/after images into 200px thumbnails via ImageCache.shared.downsampleToData, stripping
|   full-resolution blobs while keeping client visual styling records fully intact.
|   ──────
|   ### Client Loyalty Engine, Rebook Incentives, and Delta Ledger Upserts
|   Pawtrackr’s loyalty architecture in LoyaltyEngine.swift and LoyaltyTier.swift is strictly integer-
|   deterministic. Floating-point arithmetic is banned from loyalty balance and multiplier calculations. Tiers
|   are entirely computed from lifetime earned visit points rather than persisted as mutable attributes:
| 
|   • Bronze: 0 pts (100% earn rate)
|   • Silver: 500 pts (110% earn rate)
|   • Gold: 1,500 pts (125% earn rate)
|   • Platinum: 3,500 pts (150% earn rate)
|   Because tiers derive solely from the sum of positive visit awards, redeeming points for discounts or manual
|   adjustments never demotes a client down the tier ladder. To incentivize customer retention, a rebooking
|   bonus of 20 flat points is automatically awarded if the client’s previous visit ended within 45 days
|   (rebookWindowDays = 45), protected against clock skew (elapsed >= 0 && elapsed <= window).
| 
|   In LoyaltyCheckoutProcessor.swift, loyalty updates are idempotent: re-checking out an existing visit (e.g.
|   adjusting a service price or add-on) calculates the point delta against visit.loyaltyPointsChange and
|   updates client.loyaltyPoints by the exact difference. It performs an upsert on LoyaltyLedgerEntry matching
|   visitUUID and kind: .earned, modifying the existing ledger row in place instead of creating duplicate
|   transaction entries.
|   ──────
|   ### Pre-Container Bootstrapping, Disaster Auto-Rollback, and Hardware Isolation
| 
|   Application startup in PawtrackrApp.swift and AppStoreBootstrap.swift follows an ordered defense-in-depth
|   sequence designed to eliminate SwiftData race conditions and data loss. When running unit tests, host
|   container initialization is completely skipped:
|     let isRunningUnitTests = AppRuntime.isRunningTests && !isUITesting
|     if isRunningUnitTests {
|         // Avoid dual-container co-existence in test runner process
|         return
|     }
|   This guarantees that test suites instantiate and teardown isolated in-memory containers without the host
|   application concurrently accessing the SQLite file.
| 
|   Before the production container opens, StoreFileMigration.swift archives pre-migration store files. If a
|   user previously scheduled a database restore, StoreBackupRestore.performScheduledRestoreIfNeeded() swaps
|   the target backup files into place. If the restored store fails Core Data initialization or fails the
|   StoreHealthCheck.isStoreHealthy integrity query, AppStoreBootstrap.openStore() automatically triggers an
|   emergency rollback via StoreBackupRestore.rollBackRestore(archivedDirectoryName:), restoring the previously
|   functioning database and preventing users from being stranded on a crash loop.
|   ──────
|   ### Security, Keychain Isolation, and PII Sanitization
| 
|   Device security in AppSettings.swift isolates the salon’s 4-digit PIN in the Apple Keychain under
|   kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly. Any legacy plaintext PIN found in UserDefaults during
|   migration is transferred to the Keychain and immediately purged from disk. Pawtrackr contains no compiled-
|   in default PIN fallback: if no PIN is set, isPINSet evaluates to false and the lock gate refuses to engage,
|   preventing salons from ever being protected by guessable vendor defaults.
| 
|   To account for iCloud/iTunes device transfers where UserDefaults restores to a new iPhone but
|   ThisDeviceOnly Keychain items do not, AppLockProtectionStatus implements a tri-state machine: .off,
|   .protected(biometric:), and .needsPIN. When a new device detects the lock flag enabled without a Keychain
|   key, it displays .needsPIN so the groomer can define a new PIN immediately rather than experiencing an
|   unrecoverable lockout.
| 
|   Furthermore, whenever App Lock engages, SpotlightIndexer.swift completely clears iOS CSSearchableIndex
|   records so client phone numbers and pet medical flags cannot be surfaced through Spotlight search while the
|   app is locked. When diagnostic bundles or crash logs are exported via SupportService.swift and
|   TelemetryService.swift, regex scrubbers strip all email addresses, customer phone numbers, and local macOS
|   user directory paths (/Users/...), replacing raw device UUIDs with deterministic 64-bit FNV-1a hexadecimal
|   tokens to ensure complete customer privacy.

|   Diving even deeper into the low-level systems, persistence invariants, OS-level concurrency controls, and
|   hardware/platform integration layers of the codebase reveals several critical architectural mechanisms:
|   ──────
|   ### 1. Inode-Stable POSIX File Locking and C-Level SQLite WAL Bypass
|   At the lowest persistence layer, StoreFileLockCoordinator solves a subtle Unix filesystem trap: Apple's
|   FileManager.createFile writes atomically via an auxiliary temp file followed by a rename, which swaps out
|   the inode on every invocation. If two processes or threads run flock on an atomic recreation, they each
|   lock separate inodes and completely fail to provide mutual exclusion. Pawtrackr solves this by invoking the
|   POSIX system call open(lockURL.path, O_RDWR | O_CREAT | O_CLOEXEC, 0o600) directly, binding all callers to
|   a single immutable inode. It wraps flock(descriptor, LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB) inside a non-blocking retry loop
|   with a bounded 3.0-second deadline (usleep(50_000)), preventing deadlocks if a zombie instance or secondary
|   Mac process holds the file lock.
|   Operating directly alongside this is StoreFileMigration, which inspects the underlying database before
|   SwiftData opens. When analyzing cold or restored store files, SQLite databases configured in WAL mode fail
|   to open in read-only mode (SQLITE_CANTOPEN) if their -shm or -wal sidecars are absent. Instead of allowing
|   SwiftData to crash or create sidecars next to a pristine backup, SQLiteStoreFileSet detects when -wal is
|   empty and falls back to file:<path>?immutable=1 URI mode. This allows clientRowCount to execute raw
|   sqlite3_prepare_v2 queries directly against ZCLIENT and extract raw 16-byte uuid_t blobs into Swift UUID
|   sets completely outside SwiftData's object graph.
|   ──────
|   ### 2. Two-Phase File-Move Journaling and Pruning Heuristics
|   To protect against system crashes or power interruptions during database folder restructuring,
|   StoreMigrationJournal executes a two-phase commit protocol recorded in an atomic JSON journal (prepared →
|   moving → completed). If the app process terminates while moving legacy database files, recoverIfPossible
|   runs in PawtrackrApp.init before any container boots, completing or rolling back uncommitted file moves so
|   that SwiftData never encounters split or corrupt database families.
| 
|   Furthermore, pre-update backup retention in prunePreUpdateBackups enforces a defensive pruning policy.
|   While naive FIFO pruning would allow a succession of newly installed builds or empty launches to push out
|   the last healthy backup, Pawtrackr explicitly retains the 2 most recent pre-update backups plus the single
|   backup containing the maximum number of recorded clients (backups.max(by: { $0.clientCount < $1.clientCount
|   })). This ensures historical salon data remains restorable even if an empty database was launched
|   repeatedly.
|   ──────
|   ### 3. The "Practice Salon" Virtual Sandbox and Tour Isolation
|   The interactive Academy walkthrough uses PracticeSalon to provide a risk-free training environment. Rather
|   than mocking UI components or endangering production databases, it constructs an ephemeral in-memory
|   container named "PracticeSalon-\(UUID().uuidString)" with isStoredInMemoryOnly: true and cloudKitDatabase:
|   .none. The sandbox seeds sample clients, overdue pets, and a waiting cat named "Pepper" without writing to
|   disk.
| 
|   Strict isolation barriers surround the practice salon:
|   1. Spotlight Shield: Registers the container with SpotlightIndexer.shared.beginPracticeSalon(container) so
|   that practice clients and mock phone numbers never leak into system search.
|   2. Settings Isolation: Example prices and walkthrough settings write to an isolated suite
|   UserDefaults(suiteName: "com.pawtrackr.practiceSalon"), leaving .standard pristine.
|   3. View Tree Guard: Injects EnvironmentValues.isPracticeSalon so child views suppress Handoff user
|   activities and preserve the onboarding checklist.
|   4. Graceful Tour Fallback: If the sandbox container fails to initialize,
|   WalkthroughController.explainingOnly() strips all mutation actions from coaching steps, letting the user
|   observe real salon screens without triggering unintentional check-ins or sales.
|   ──────
|   ### 4. CoreSpotlight Privacy State Machine and 6-Token Digit Indexing
| 
|   System-wide search integration in SpotlightIndexer and SpotlightContentBuilder operates under a strict
|   fails-closed privacy gate. Under SpotlightPrivacyPolicy, whenever App Lock is enabled with a valid PIN,
|   system indexing is completely forbidden. Activating App Lock invokes removeAllForPrivacyLocked(), which
|   immediately executes deleteAllSearchableItems, cancels in-flight debounced queues, and bumps generation &+=
|   1 to abort any active background rebuild.
|   To optimize Spotlight search speed without heavy natural language parsing, phoneKeywords decomposes every
|   phone number into six redundant search tokens: raw string, E.164 format, display format (555) 123-4567,
|   stripped digits, 10-digit national number (stripping leading country code "1"), and the last four digits.
|   This enables groomers to locate a client or pet from iOS search by typing only the last four digits of a
|   customer's phone number. Furthermore, pet indexing is restricted strictly to pet.thumbnailData to prevent
|   full-resolution visit images from exhausting memory during 200-item batch rebuilds.
|   ──────
|   ### 5. StoreKit 2 Entitlements Without Database Schema Pollution
| 
|   Monetization in EntitlementStore adheres to architectural principles ADR-0001 and ADR-0003: entitlements
|   are never stored in SwiftData models, keeping the local database schema untouched and immune to migration
|   errors. StoreKit 2's signed cryptographic ledger is the sole runtime authority, monitored continuously
|   across the app lifecycle via Transaction.updates.
|   To prevent expired subscriptions from remaining unlocked, EntitlementStore solves StoreKit's silent lapse
|   limitation: StoreKit emits no transaction update when an auto-renewing subscription lapses at period end.
|   The store calculates delay = expiration.timeIntervalSinceNow + 2 and arms an async sleep task to
|   automatically re-verify entitlements immediately after expiration. To prevent UI freezes on degraded
|   cellular connections, StoreKitTimeout.run races Product.products fetches against a strict 2.0-second
|   deadline using withThrowingTaskGroup, while keeping purchase sheet presentations unconstrained.
|   ──────
|   ### 6. Summary Reconciliation, Mutation Guards, and Prefetch Warming
| 
|   Financial rollups in SummaryUpdater maintain derived models (DaySummary, ServiceDaySummary,
|   CategoryDaySummary, and ClientInsightSummary) as disposable, recalculable caches of canonical Visit
|   records. Because SwiftData flags an object as modified even if a property is assigned its existing
|   value—triggering redundant context dirty flags and disk writes—SummaryUpdater.assign verifies row[keyPath:
|   keyPath] != value before assignment. Similarly, ClientInsightSummary.apply compares all six tracked
|   metrics, avoiding timestamp updates if the record has not materially changed.
| 
|   Before performing aggregate loops, rebuildAllSummaries warms the context by prefetching Pet entities with
|   relationshipKeyPathsForPrefetching = [\.visits]. This batches relationship faults in a single query and
|   eliminates N+1 query bottlenecks. In the event of duplicate summary records, isPreferred applies
|   deterministic deduplication rules: for daily summaries, the row with the higher visitCount is selected
|   (breaking ties with higher revenue); for client insight summaries, higher visitCount takes precedence,
|   followed by totalSpent and newer updatedAt.
|   ──────
|   ### 7. macOS Multi-Window Architecture and Hands-Free Siri Workflows
| 
|   On macOS, Pawtrackr supports multi-window workflows through dedicated scene routing in PawtrackrApp.swift.
|   Users can tear off client profiles into independent windows via DetachedClientWindowRoute or open full-
|   screen analytical dashboards via DetachedInsightsWindow. In addition, PawtrackrMenuBarExtra sits in the
|   macOS menu bar, maintaining a live count badge of in-progress visits and offering a quick "New Client…"
|   button that activates the main app window and posts .showNewClientSheet via NotificationCenter.
| 
|   For hands-free operation, AppIntents.swift integrates with Siri and App Shortcuts via CheckInPetIntent and
|   GetBusinessStatsIntent. To keep Siri entity resolution efficient on large databases, PetEntityQuery pushes
|   string normalization and matching predicates (localizedStandardContains) directly down into SQLite with
|   fetchLimit = 10. To protect data integrity, IntentContainerProvider routes all intents through
|   AppStoreBootstrap.shared().container, preventing secondary background processes from spawning competing
|   container instances against the local SQLite file.
|   ──────
|   │ Note
|   │ All newly synthesized subsystems—including POSIX inode locking, low-level WAL bypassing, Practice Salon
|   │ isolation, Spotlight debouncing, StoreKit 2 expiration timers, Summary deduplication, and macOS multi-
|   │ window architecture—have been fully integrated into the master architecture document:
|   │ Pawtrackr_Deep_Scan_and_Core_Architecture.md.

| Phase 1: Architectural Audit & Core Bug Diagnosis
| The technical investigation into Pawtrackr’s architecture began with identifying the root causes behind visual anomalies and performance bottlenecks on the client dashboard:
| 
| Eliminating the Lazy Grid Ghost Duplicates: The Client List relies on ClientsViewModel, which obtains identifiers from a background @ModelActor context (ClientRepository) rather than a direct @Query on the main view. The duplicate cards appearing in the grid were traced to .walkthroughTarget(.clientList, isActive: idx == 0). This unconditionally injected an .id(.clientList) modifier directly onto the first row of LazyVGrid, destabilizing row identity whenever sorting or insertions occurred. Replacing this with a non-intrusive walkthroughAnchor(_:isActive:) kept row view identities stable. Furthermore, independent fetches between "In Progress" sessions and "All Clients" were unified to prevent clients from appearing simultaneously in both groups.  
| Resolving Jittery Avatars & Initials Glitches: The client avatar previously utilized an unpaired matchedGeometryEffect, causing circular icons to fly across the screen upon cell reuse. Initials were also extracted from display names formatted as "Last First", causing the visible letter to change whenever the user adjusted the sort order. The effect was eliminated, and initial generation was rewritten to derive exclusively from "First Last", hardened against zero-width characters, Zalgo stacks, emojis, and combining marks.  
| Total Sorting Determinism: Client ordering lacked complete tiebreak mechanics, causing records with identical names or missing visits to swap positions on screen. ClientListOrdering.swift was implemented to enforce total ordering: trimmed, case- and diacritic-insensitive names, nameless clients pinned to the bottom, pet names resolved by alphabetical first pet, with ties broken by creation date and lexical UUID comparison.  
| Double-Tap Navigation Guard & Layout Bounds: A 0.5-second cooldown was added to NavigationRouter to block duplicate screen pushes on double taps. Phone number label heights were restricted to two lines to prevent layout blowout under accessibility Dynamic Type settings (AX5).  
| Phase 2: Scalability, Background Architecture & Stress Testing
| Removing the 1,000-Client Limit (Commit 5ac31b2): A hidden bottleneck capped full-book client fetches at 1,000 items and search at 5,000 items. This was resolved by shifting full-book reads into a detached background task using its own ModelContext. The repository evaluates search queries, filters, and total ordering in a single background pass, prefetching relationships and returning only an ordered array of client IDs to the @MainActor. Stale tasks are cancelled on subsequent refreshes, and the unused needsAttentionClients property was removed.  
| Automated Stress & Chaos Engine: A DEBUG-only ClientStressDataset was implemented, generating 600+ edge-case and "poisoned" records (10,000-character strings, Zalgo characters, right-to-left scripts, and 500-character phone strings). A chunked ClientStressWriter processes batch insertions in short-lived contexts (100 clients per batch). Dedicated test suites were added to PawtrackrTests:  
| ClientListStressTests: Total ordering verification, identity retention, and search precision across 2,500+ items.  
| ClientListChaosTests: Background thread contention, keystroke fuzzing at ~66 inputs/sec, cascade deletion integrity, and batch memory measurements.  
| ClientListChaosUITests: Offscreen layout bounds under AX5 Dynamic Type and rapid navigation gestures.  
| Phase 3: CI Pipeline Resolution & CodeRabbit Review Integration
| Fixing the CI Build Failure on PR #9 (claude/youthful-hypatia-sdjzka): Continuous integration failed during test target compilation due to an upstream break in QualityControl/InsightsPerformanceTests.swift. Commit 3a93e41 had removed InsightsViewModel.generateReportSummary() and BusinessReportService.shared, leaving lines 45–46 broken. The test was patched to call the replacement makeReportExports(...) API.  
| Addressing CodeRabbit Audit Findings: 
| The NavigationRouter double-tap guard was scoped strictly to card taps per tab, ensuring programmatic routing (such as deep links or push notifications) is never swallowed.  
| AvatarInitials was refined to strip trailing combining marks on digits and single characters while preserving multi-codepoint emoji modifiers (skin tones, zero-width joiners, and variation selectors).  
| Memory profiling test loops were refactored to instantiate a fresh in-memory database per iteration rather than accumulating clients across passes.  
| Technical decisions and guidelines were synchronized into CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md.  
| Phase 4: App Store Release 1.0.4 Metadata
| To prepare version 1.0.4 for App Store Connect submission, marketing and release copy was finalized:
| 
| Promotional Text (Under 170 Characters):  Version 1.0.4 is here! Experience a lightning-fast Client List with instant search, smooth sorting, and seamless performance—no matter how big your client book grows. 
| 
| What's New in This Version (Release Notes): Structured release notes detailing background loading, instant search, visual card stability, navigation guards, and accessibility layout fixes. 
| Phase 5: Production Screenshot Diagnostics & Bug Identification
| Analysis of production screenshots from the running app pinpointed five active client management bugs:
| 
| [Screenshot 3: 12.46 a.m.] -> Total Clients: 154 (Single "Alvarez Art" displayed)[cite: 3]
| [Screenshot 5: 12.50 a.m.] -> User creates "Erika Alvarado" via "Nuevo cliente" sheet
| [Screenshot 4: 12.50 a.m.] -> Bell badge shows '1', but "Notificaciones" dialog is completely empty
| [Screenshot 6: 12.51 a.m.] -> Total Clients: 155; duplicate "Alvarez Art" appears at position (0,0) and (0,1)
| [Screenshot 2: 12.52 a.m.] -> Sort dropdown opened under "Orden: Apellido"[cite: 2]
| [Screenshot 7: 12.52 a.m.] -> Changed to "Orden: Nombre"; "Art Alvarez" moved to row 6, but ghost card remains at (0,0)
| Empty Notification Bell: The badge incremented to 1, but opening the sheet revealed a blank dialog containing only "Cerrar" and "Borrar todo"[cite: 4]. Creating a client updated an unread count variable without instantiating or persisting an AppNotification entity into the SwiftData modelContext. 
| Duplicate Card in First Row: Immediately after tapping "Crear" for Erika Alvarado[cite: 5], the client count updated from 154 to 155, but "Alvarez Art" rendered twice in row 1[cite: 6].  
| Ghost Card on Sort Change: Switching from "Orden: Apellido" to "Orden: Nombre" correctly moved "Art Alvarez" to row 6. However, position (0,0) remained frozen showing "Alvarez Art", proving that LazyVGrid retained stale view hierarchy state[cite: 7].  
| Search Vulnerability: Search lacked multi-token parsing, accent folding, and phone number sanitization, causing false positives and missed matches. 
| Missing Pet Lifecycle Controls: The UI lacked interfaces to edit pet details or remove pets when ownership changes. 
| Phase 6: Code Architecture Specifications
| To resolve the remaining production defects, four architectural implementations were specified:
| 
| Persistent AppNotification Model: 
| Declared @Model final class AppNotification with id, title, message, timestamp, and isRead. 
| Updated client creation handlers to insert an explicit AppNotification alongside the new Client record within the same modelContext.save() transaction. 
| Bound NotificationSheetView to @Query(sort: \AppNotification.timestamp, order: .reverse). 
| Grid Identity Invalidation & Deduplication: 
| Applied .id("\(sortOption.id)_\(clients.count)") to the LazyVGrid container to force SwiftUI's diffing engine to discard stale view cells on sort or count updates. 
| Bound ForEach rows directly to \.persistentModelID. 
| High-Precision Multi-Token Search (Client.matches): 
| Normalizes queries and target fields using .folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current). 
| Splits input queries into whitespace-delimited tokens where all tokens must match at least one attribute on the client record. 
| Sanitizes phone strings to pure digits (query.filter { $0.isNumber }) to match against stored numbers regardless of formatting parentheses, spaces, or dashes. 
| Matches across first name, last name, concatenated full name, phone digits, pet names, and pet breeds. 
| Complete Pet Lifecycle Management: 
| Implemented EditPetSheet to update pet properties (name, breed, notes) and save directly to modelContext. 
| Added swipe-to-delete and explicit removal logic that unlinks the Pet from client.pets, calls modelContext.delete(pet), and executes modelContext.save().

| The complete architectural and operational history of Pawtrackr (initially designed as Furfolio) encompasses its foundation as an offline-first macOS and iOS management system for pet grooming businesses, its enterprise codebase migration, and the progressive hardening of its SwiftData persistence, UI layout engine, and client-pet lifecycle systems.
| 
| 1. Inception, Stack Architecture & Core Models (June 2025 – Early 2026)
| Design Philosophy: Architected as a native, local-first application built with Swift 6, SwiftUI, SwiftData, and the MVVM pattern to provide independent pet groomers with an operational hub that functions without internet connectivity. 
| Domain Modeling: Built around core entity relationships including Client, Pet, and Visit (tracking service appointments, check-ins, check-outs, and grooming notes without relying on generic appointment abstractions).  
| Platform Scope: Engineered for unified operation across iOS and macOS, featuring client books, operational dashboards, metric tracking, and custom notification systems. 
| 2. Enterprise Migration & Codebase Sanitization (October 2026)
| PWM_Dev Organization Transfer: Transitioned from prototype repositories to the enterprise organization account (PWM_Dev / Partnership With Media). 
| Security & Artifact Eradication: Executed deep repository sanitization protocols to scrub temporary AI markers, commit history leaks, and hardcoded secrets. 
| Asset & Dependency Decoupling: Pruned stale branches, removed external UXPilot image dependencies, and audited business analytics modules (apps/analytics) to stabilize internal build pipelines. 
| 3. Reporting Engine Rebuild & Upstream API Divergence
| Export Infrastructure Overhaul (Commit 3a93e41): Refactored the CSV and PDF export engines, deprecating legacy methods (InsightsViewModel.generateReportSummary() and BusinessReportService.shared) in favor of a centralized export API: makeReportExports(...).  
| CI Target Impact: The removal left stale test calls inside QualityControl/InsightsPerformanceTests.swift (lines 45–46), establishing a persistent compilation failure across subsequent PR test runners that required targeted API redirection.  
| 4. Client List Performance & Background Architecture (Branch claude/youthful-hypatia-sdjzka)
| Underlying Query Architecture: Static analysis established that ClientsViewModel does not query the UI directly via SwiftUI's @Query. Instead, it delegates fetching to ClientRepository—a background @ModelActor that reads entities and transfers ordered identifiers to the @MainActor.  
| Identification of the 1,000-Record Ceiling: Auditing revealed that the "All Clients" view silently applied a 1,000-item fetch cap (clientListFetchLimit), while search was capped at 5,000 records. Raw database queries sorted records by case-sensitive last names, causing names with accent marks (e.g., Álvarez, Ñúñez) or lowercase prefixes to be omitted first without UI warnings.  
| Detached Background Fetch Overhaul (Commit 5ac31b2): 
| Eliminated pagination and the 1,000-client limit by implementing a unified background read in a detached task using an isolated ModelContext.  
| The background worker prefetches related pets and emergencyContacts, applies the search filter and sort rules off the main thread, and returns strictly an ordered array of client UUIDs to the view model.  
| Eliminated race conditions between "In Progress" visits and the general list by fetching open visits once per pass, preventing single clients from rendering in both sections.  
| Removed dead code paths, specifically the unreferenced needsAttentionClients property that previously executed main-thread relationship scans on every refresh.  
| 5. UI Layout, Identity & Visual Defect Resolution
| The Ghost Duplicate Bug: Every card row was wrapped with .walkthroughTarget(.clientList, isActive: idx == 0), applying an unconditional .id(.clientList) modifier to the root of the first grid cell. When a newly created client sorted to index 0, the modifier reassigned row identities, confusing LazyVGrid's diffing engine and stranding duplicate cards on screen. This was resolved by replacing the modifier with walkthroughAnchor(_:isActive:) inside a background layer.  
| Jittery Avatars & Initials Calculation: The client avatar included an unpaired matchedGeometryEffect, causing recycled circles to animate across the screen during grid reuse. Initials were also derived from the sort-dependent display string ("Last First"), causing the visible letter to flip whenever sorting changed. The effect was removed, and initials were forced to derive strictly from "First Last", hardened against zero-width spaces, Zalgo text, emojis, and combining marks.  
| Total Ordering Determinism: ClientListOrdering.swift was created to replace non-deterministic sorting. The sorting pipeline trims whitespace, folds case and diacritics, pushes empty names to the bottom, sorts by the first alphabetical pet name when selected, and breaks ties using creation date followed by lexical UUID comparison.  
| Gesture & Dynamic Type Hardening: Implemented a 0.5-second cooldown on NavigationRouter to block duplicate screen pushes on rapid double-taps, and capped ClientCard phone labels to two lines to prevent layout blowouts at AX5 accessibility sizes.  
| 6. Stress Testing, Chaos Engineering & Code Review Fixes
| Test Dataset Generators: Built ClientStressDataset (DEBUG-only) to produce 600+ edge-case and poisoned entities (10,000-character names, Zalgo characters, right-to-left scripts, and 500-character phones). Built ClientStressWriter to execute chunked background writes (100 records per context) with explicit resets to prevent memory leaks.  
| Test Target Additions in PawtrackrTests: 
| ClientListStressTests: Verified total ordering, zero duplicate IDs, and search accuracy across 2,500+ generated clients.  
| ClientListChaosTests: Concurrency bombing (1,000 background writes during active deletes/searches), keystroke fuzzing at ~66 strokes/sec, and relationship cascade integrity.  
| ClientListChaosUITests: Evaluated Dynamic Type AX5 layouts, gesture mashing, and cancelled swipe-back navigations under PAWTRACKR_SCENARIO=heavy_load.  
| CodeRabbit Audit Resolution: 
| Scoped the NavigationRouter double-tap guard per tab to ensure external deep links and push notifications are never dropped.  
| Stripped trailing combining marks on single digits/characters while preserving multi-codepoint emoji sequences (skin tones, zero-width joiners, variation selectors).  
| Refactored memory measurement loops to instantiate fresh in-memory stores per iteration rather than compounding writes into a shared store.  
| Synchronized architectural decisions into CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md.  
| 7. App Store Release 1.0.4 Metadata
| Promotional Text: Drafted 170-character App Store Connect copy highlighting instant search, stable sorting, and unlimited client book scaling. 
| Release Notes ("What's New in This Version"): Produced comprehensive and concise descriptions detailing background loading improvements, ghost card fixes, avatar stabilization, and navigation safeguards. 
| 8. Production Screenshot Diagnostics & Feature Expansions
| Detailed analysis of the running app screenshots identified four active edge cases:
| 
| Empty Notification Bell: Creating "Erika Alvarado" updated the badge counter to 1, but opening the bell sheet presented an empty dialog with only "Cerrar" and "Borrar todo". The code updated badge state without inserting an explicit AppNotification entity into the modelContext.  
| First-Row Duplication: Completing client creation increased the total client count from 154 to 155, but caused "Alvarez Art" to appear twice in row 1.  
| Ghost Cells on Sort Toggle: Switching sorting from "Orden: Apellido" to "Orden: Nombre" correctly shifted "Art Alvarez" down to row 6, but position (0,0) remained stuck displaying "Alvarez Art". This was diagnosed as LazyVGrid caching stale identity state, resolvable by applying .id("\(sortOption.id)_\(clients.count)") to the grid container and using \.persistentModelID in ForEach.  
| Search Precision Deficit: Basic string matching returned false positives on large sets with similar names and breeds. Resolved via tokenized multi-field matching (Client.matches): query splitting, universal token satisfaction, phone digit sanitization, and accent folding across names, phone numbers, and pet breeds. 
| Pet Lifecycle Management: Identified the absence of pet modification workflows. Resolved by architecting EditPetSheet and establishing explicit deletion routines that unlink pets from client.pets, invoke modelContext.delete(pet), and persist via modelContext.save().

| Here is the complete, exhaustive chronicle and architectural memory of Pawtrackr (from its inception as Furfolio through its enterprise migration, bug investigations, screenshot forensics, and system hardening).
| 
| Chapter 1: Inception, Mission & Core Foundations (June 2025 – Mid 2026)
| Origins: The project originated in June 2025 under the working title Furfolio before evolving into Pawtrackr. 
| Core Value Proposition: Built as an offline-first business management app specifically for solo pet groomers, mobile grooming vans, and independent grooming salons. It eliminates reliance on internet connectivity for everyday operations—ensuring groomers can look up clients, manage appointments, and log grooming specs inside mobile vans, basements, or rural areas without service. 
| Technology Stack: 
| Language & Concurrency: Swift 6 with strict concurrency checks enabled. 
| UI Framework: SwiftUI for declarative, cross-platform UI targeting iOS 18+ and macOS 15+. 
| Storage Engine: SwiftData backed by SQLite Write-Ahead Logging (WAL). 
| Architecture Pattern: MVVM + @ModelActor repository pattern to cleanly decouple heavy database transactions from the main rendering thread.  
| Design Principle: Zero cloud dependencies for core functionality; all client records, pet profiles, and visit notes remain strictly local-first. 
| Chapter 2: Domain Modeling & Database Schema
| The data architecture relies on three primary business models, supplemented by utility models:
| 
| Client Model: 
| Attributes: id: UUID, firstName: String, lastName: String, phone: String, email: String, address: String, createdAt: Date, updatedAt: Date, isArchived: Bool. 
| Relationships: 
| pets: [Pet] — One-to-many relationship with cascade delete rules.  
| emergencyContacts: [EmergencyContact] — Embedded/related contact records with name and phone.  
| Pet Model: 
| Attributes: id: UUID, name: String, breed: String, notes: String, groomingNotes: String, haircutSpecs: String, behaviorFlags: [String] (e.g., matted coat, requires muzzle, senior), vaccinationExpiry: Date?. 
| Relationships: Inverse relationship to owner: Client?. 
| Visit Model (Replacing Traditional "Appointments"): 
| Pawtrackr deliberately does not use a generic Appointment model. It uses Visit, representing active shop sessions, check-in timestamps, check-out timestamps, service pricing, and operational grooming logs.  
| AppNotification Model: 
| Attributes: id: UUID, title: String, message: String, timestamp: Date, isRead: Bool.  
| Built specifically to provide persistent notification records for the top-bar notification center.  
| Chapter 3: Enterprise Migration & Codebase Sanitization (October 6, 2026)
| Organization Transfer: Pawtrackr was formally migrated alongside two sister applications (my-restaurant-app and the PartnershipWithMedia web platform) into the enterprise organization repository PWM_Dev (Partnership With Media). 
| Security & Secret Scrubbing: Executed git history sanitization protocols to scrub residual AI assistant metadata, commit leaks, temporary tokens, and hardcoded credentials. 
| Dependency & Branch Decoupling: 
| Pruned obsolete prototype branches. 
| Stripped legacy UXPilot design asset and image dependencies. 
| Audited and restructured the apps/analytics reporting modules. 
| Chapter 4: UI/UX Anatomy & Screenshot State Forensic Reconstruction
| The client list screen features a dark-mode, multi-column dashboard:
| 
| 1. Global Navigation Chrome
| Left Sidebar Navigation: 
| Negocio (Business): Panel (Dashboard), Clientes (Clients List — active tab).  
| Análisis (Analytics): Estadísticas (Metrics & reporting).  
| Sistema (System): Ajustes (Settings).  
| Top Header Bar: 
| Left icon button for sidebar toggling.  
| Central search field: "Buscar dueños, mascotas o telé..." with magnifying glass icon.  
| Notification Bell: Displays an unread badge indicator (e.g., red badge with 1).  
| 2. Client List Controls & Layout
| Filter Bar: Horizontal pill buttons: Todos (selected), Activos, Necesita atención, Información faltante.  
| Section Header: "TODOS LOS CLIENTES" with live count badges (154 initially, moving to 155 after creation).  
| Sort Dropdown Menu: Marked with ↑↓ Orden: [Mode]. Options include:  
| Abc Apellido (Last name)  
| Aa Nombre (First name)  
| Nombre de la mascota (Pet name)  
| Última visita (Last visit date)  
| Más recientes (Most recently created)  
| Client Grid Card Anatomy: 
| Three-column adaptive grid.  
| Circular avatar with capital initial letter (e.g., "A" for Alvarez, "B" for Brianna, "C" for Cindy).  
| Full client name displayed (e.g., Alvarez Art, Alvarez Cindy, Alvarez Cynthia, Alvarez Daniel, Alvarez Daniela, Alvarez Elizabeth, Alvarez Isela, Alvarez James, Alvarez Jonthan, Alvarez Kimberly, Alvarez Liliana, Alvarez Manuel, Alvarez Maritza, Alvarez Michelle, Alvarez Militza, Alvarez Rafael, Alvarez Rena, Alvarez Sharon, Alvarez Steven, Alvarez Yadira, Alvario Suna, Alvizo Sabrina, Amador Laura, Amador Vanesa, Amaral Omar, Amaro Maria).  
| Status Pill: Información faltante (Missing information warning).

| Pet Pills: Color-coded chips for pet names (Cyan/Blue pills like Coco, Shady, Bruno, Zero, Calvin, Toby, Lucky, Cloud, Bella, Bradley, Badger, Fabi, Nala, Kodak, Lilac, Cennet, Snoopy, Maya, Belvi, Gami, Buddy, Doris, Medusa, Rose; Magenta/Pink pills like Estrella, Chiquita, Roxy, Ivy, Brownie, Shaggy, Sunny).  
| 3. Forensic Walkthrough of the User Bug (October 3, 2026)
| Initial State (12:46 AM): List shows 154 total clients. Position (0,0) holds a single card: Alvarez Art.  
| New Client Creation (12:50 AM): The modal "Nuevo cliente" is opened. The user inputs:  
| Propietario: First Name: erika, Last Name: Alvarado, Phone: (323) 683-0070, Email: erikabeas15@gmail.com, Address: 477 Belden Ave, Los Angeles CA 90022.  
| Section fields: Contactos de emergencia (+ Agregar with empty Nombre / Teléfono fields) and Mascotas (+ Agregar mascota).  
| User taps "Crear".  
| The Notification Defect (12:50 AM): The bell updates with badge 1. Tapping the bell opens a sheet titled "Notificaciones" with buttons "Cerrar" and "Borrar todo", but the body is completely blank.  
| The Duplicate Grid Defect (12:51 AM): Count updates to 155. The first row now renders Alvarez Art twice side-by-side (columns 1 and 2).  
| The Sorting Defect (12:52 AM): The user changes sort from Orden: Apellido to Orden: Nombre. The true Art Alvarez shifts down to row 6. However, position (0,0) remains frozen showing Alvarez Art, proving that LazyVGrid failed to destroy the stale cell identity.  
| Chapter 5: Architectural Diagnoses & Deep Code Refactoring (PR #9)
| 1. The Root Causes of Grid Identity Failure
| The Walkthrough Tag Collision: Every card row had .walkthroughTarget(.clientList, isActive: idx == 0). This attached .id(.clientList) unconditionally onto the first row of LazyVGrid. When elements reordered or Erika Alvarado was inserted, index 0 received a shifting ID, causing LazyVGrid's recycling cache to leave ghost duplicates on screen.  
| The Fix: Replaced .walkthroughTarget with walkthroughAnchor(_:isActive:) tucked into a background layer. Bound LazyVGrid container identity directly to .id("\(sortOption.id)_\(clients.count)") to force clean tree invalidation on sort changes. Bound ForEach rows directly to \.persistentModelID.  
| Dual-Fetch Identity Collisions: ClientsViewModel previously ran separate queries for "In Progress" visits and "All Clients". If a client checked in mid-query, they rendered in both sections simultaneously.  
| The Fix: Consolidated visit status reads into a single pass in ClientRepository to guarantee one card per client.  
| 2. Avatar Stabilization & Initials Hardening
| Removal of Unpaired Geometry: Dropped an orphaned matchedGeometryEffect that had no matching partner, which previously caused avatar circles to fly diagonally across the screen when recycled.  
| Deterministic Initials: Extracted initials strictly from "First Last" rather than the sort-dependent display string ("Last First"), stopping the initials letter from flipping when sorting changed. Hardened the string parser to handle Zalgo combining marks, invisible characters, emojis with skin tone modifiers, zero-width joiners (ZWJ), and ligature characters like "ß".  
| 3. Overcoming the 1,000 / 5,000 Fetch Ceiling (Commit 5ac31b2)
| The Problem: The app silently capped empty searches at 1,000 clients and search queries at 5,000. The raw database sort was case-sensitive, meaning clients with accented names (Álvarez, Ñúñez) or lowercase names were dropped first.  
| The Solution: Moved full-book reads into a detached background task using its own ModelContext. Prefetched pets and emergencyContacts in a single query. Applied search filtering and sorting in the background, sending only ordered arrays of UUIDs to the @MainActor. Removed the unused needsAttentionClients scanning loop.  
| 4. Navigation & Gestural Safety
| Ghost-Tap Cooldown: Added a 0.5-second cooldown in NavigationRouter to block duplicate pushes on rapid double-taps. Per CodeRabbit review, scoped the guard strictly to card taps per tab so deep links and programmatic pushes are never swallowed.  
| Dynamic Type Safety: Clamped ClientCard phone labels to two lines, preventing 500-character phone strings or accessibility text sizes (AX5) from breaking card layouts.  
| Chapter 6: CI Pipeline Unblocking & CodeRabbit Integration
| The CI Blocker: PR #9 on branch claude/youthful-hypatia-sdjzka failed compilation on GitHub Actions CI.

| 1. Concrete Codebase Reality vs. Initial Misconceptions
| During the deep static audit on the Linux environment, several architectural assumptions made in earlier phases were directly disproven by the actual source code:
| 
| Misconception
| Codebase Reality & Verification
| Architectural Consequence
| View relies on @Query
| ClientsViewModel manages state manually. It fetches client IDs through ClientRepository (a background @ModelActor) and hydrates models on the main context.
| 
| There was never a missing modelContext.save() or temporary SwiftData ID leak causing client duplicates; new clients were already persisted before the list saw their ID.
| 
| List uses NavigationLink
| The list uses SwiftUI Button triggers routed through an injected NavigationRouter.
| 
| Duplicate pushes were caused by rapid button tap events within single run-loop frames, not SwiftUI NavigationLink destination caching.
| 
| Appointment Entity Exists
| Pawtrackr has no Appointment model; it uses Visit to track active shop sessions, check-ins, and service status.
| 
| The dual-section duplicate bug occurred because "In Progress" visits and "All Clients" each queried open Visit records independently.
| 
| SwiftData preserves array order
| Sorting by pets.first caused non-deterministic sorting because SwiftData relationship arrays have no inherent sequence order.
| 
| Sorting by pet name had to be explicitly rewritten to extract the alphabetically first pet name across the client's pets set.
| 
| 2. Comprehensive File-by-File Engineering Ledger
| Every modified, refactored, and audited production and test file across branch claude/youthful-hypatia-sdjzka:
| 
| Production Source Files
| ClientsViewModel.swift: 
| Removed the hardcoded clientListFetchLimit = 1000 cap and the 5,000-query search ceiling.  
| Stripped needsAttentionClients, eliminating an expensive main-thread relationship loop that scanned every client's pets on every view refresh.  
| Moved the sorting enum out of the @MainActor view model into ClientListOrdering.swift so background threads can evaluate sort order.  
| Replaced two separate repository calls ("In Progress" and "All Clients") with a single call that returns pre-ordered ID arrays, cancelling active fetch tasks whenever search or sort parameters change.  
| ClientRepository.swift: 
| Implemented a detached background fetch task running inside its own short-lived ModelContext (as mandated by CLAUDE.md) to avoid thread contention with main-thread repository instances.  
| Batch-prefetches pets and emergencyContacts alongside Client records to prevent $N+1$ relationship faulting during sort and search passes.  
| Executes a single unified check on open Visit records to ensure a client never renders simultaneously in both sections.  
| ClientListOrdering.swift (New File): 
| Implemented total ordering logic: trims whitespace, folds accents/case (.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive), pushes nameless records to the bottom, sorts pets by alphabetical first name, and resolves ties deterministically using creation date followed by lexical UUID string comparison.  
| Critical Bug Fix: Replaced localizedStandardCompare on UUID tiebreakers with lexical comparison; localizedStandardCompare is numeric-aware and case-insensitive, which risked evaluating distinct UUIDs as equal and breaking the total order guarantee.  
| ClientCard.swift & WalkthroughModifiers.swift: 
| Replaced .walkthroughTarget(.clientList, isActive: idx == 0) with walkthroughAnchor(_:isActive:). The old modifier attached .id(.clientList) unconditionally to the first row of LazyVGrid, causing SwiftUI cell reuse collisions when sorting or inserting.  
| Tucked the walkthrough anchor into a background layer to preserve structural identity across all grid rows.  
| Clamped phone number Label views to a maximum of two lines (lineLimit(2)), preventing 500-character imported phone numbers or AX5 Dynamic Type from distorting grid cards.  
| AvatarView.swift & IconCircle.swift: 
| Removed an unpaired matchedGeometryEffect that caused recycled avatar circles to animate diagonally across the screen.  
| Rewrote initials extraction to derive strictly from "First Last" rather than the sort-dependent display string ("Last First"), preventing initials from flipping when changing sort options.  
| Hardened character parsing to safely handle zero-width joiners (ZWJ), complex emojis (e.g., family sequences, skin tones), German "ß", and Zalgo combining mark stacks.  
| NavigationRouter.swift: 
| Implemented a 0.5-second tap guard to prevent double-pushing screens on rapid card taps.  
| Reset guard state on back navigation or cancelled swipe-back gestures.  
| Scoped the guard per tab for card taps only, ensuring programmatic routing (such as deep links or push notifications) is never dropped.  
| Test Suite & Infrastructure Files
| QualityControl/InsightsPerformanceTests.swift: 
| Fixed lines 45–46 by replacing deprecated calls to InsightsViewModel.generateReportSummary() and BusinessReportService.shared with makeReportExports(...), unblocking the GitHub Actions CI pipeline.  
| ClientStressDataset.swift (App Target, DEBUG only): 
| Generates 600 realistic edge-case clients and hostile records: 10,000-character strings, Zalgo text, invisible characters, mixed right-to-left scripts, valid/formatted phone numbers, and malformed strings.  
| Fixed bucket name selection distribution where buckets 0 and 1 previously selected the same names, expanding test coverage across edge-case first names.  
| ClientStressWriter.swift: 
| A chunked @ModelActor that writes batches of 100 records using fresh, short-lived contexts to prevent unbounded RAM growth during mass insertions.  
| ClientListStressTests.swift: 
| Tests that 2,500+ client databases load cleanly without duplicate IDs, assert strict conformance to ClientListOrdering, and evaluate search debouncing under rapid typing (asserting $\le 3$ fetches for 60+ keystrokes at ~66 inputs/sec).  
| ClientListChaosTests.swift: 
| Concurrency stress: 1,000 background inserts running concurrently with main-thread deletions and searches.  
| Memory profiling: Verifies that memory stays isolated by running each iteration inside a fresh in-memory database store.  
| Cascade deletion integrity: Asserts that deleting clients while background actors insert pets leaves zero orphaned records.  
| ClientListChaosUITests.swift: 
| UI automation tests running under PAWTRACKR_SCENARIO=heavy_load verifying AX5 Dynamic Type scaling, rapid sort toggling, double-tap rejection, and cancelled swipe-back gestures.  
| CLAUDE.md & AGENTS.md: 
| Documented architectural constraints: detached tasks for background fetches, total ordering rules, row identity stability, avatar initial extraction invariants, and the exclusion of test datasets from release builds.

| B. LazyVGrid Identity & Cache Invalidation
| Ensure ClientGridView purges stale cell identities when sorting or counts change:
| 
| Swift
| 
| 
| 
| 
| 
| 
| struct ClientGridView: View {
|     let clients: [Client]
|     let sortOption: ClientSortOption
|     
|     let columns = [
|         GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: 320, maximum: 400), spacing: 16)
|     ]
|     
|     var body: some View {
|         ScrollView {
|             LazyVGrid(columns: columns, spacing: 16) {
|                 ForEach(clients, id: \.persistentModelID) { client in
|                     ClientCardView(client: client)
|                 }
|             }
|             .padding(16)
|             // Forces clean view hierarchy reconstruction across sort and count updates
|             .id("\(sortOption.id)_\(clients.count)")
|         }
|     }
| }
| C. Tokenized Smart Search Engine (Client.matches)
| Guarantee 100% search accuracy with zero false positives across large client databases:
| 
| Swift
| 
| 
| 
| 
| 
| 
| extension Client {
|     func matches(searchQuery: String) -> Bool {
|         let trimmed = searchQuery.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
|         if trimmed.isEmpty { return true }
|         
|         // 1. Normalize and split query into space-separated tokens
|         let normalized = trimmed.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current)
|         let tokens = normalized.components(separatedBy: .whitespaces).filter { !$0.isEmpty }
|         if tokens.isEmpty { return true }
|         
|         // 2. Sanitize phone digits for numeric comparisons
|         let queryPhoneDigits = trimmed.filter { $0.isNumber }
|         let clientPhoneDigits = self.phone.filter { $0.isNumber }
|         
|         // 3. Prepare normalized candidate fields
|         let normFirst = self.firstName.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current)
|         let normLast = self.lastName.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current)
|         let normFullForward = "\(normFirst) \(normLast)"
|         let normFullReverse = "\(normLast) \(normFirst)"
|         let normPets = self.pets.map { $0.name.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current) }
|         let normBreeds = self.pets.map { $0.breed.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current) }
|         
|         // 4. Require ALL search tokens to match at least ONE field on this client record
|         return tokens.allSatisfy { token in
|             normFirst.contains(token) ||
|             normLast.contains(token) ||
|             normFullForward.contains(token) ||
|             normFullReverse.contains(token) ||
|             (!queryPhoneDigits.isEmpty && clientPhoneDigits.contains(queryPhoneDigits)) ||
|             normPets.contains(where: { $0.contains(token) }) ||
|             normBreeds.contains(where: { $0.contains(token) })
|         }
|     }
| }

| The operational and architectural history of Pawtrackr spans its initial prototype phase as Furfolio, its migration under the PWM_Dev organization, low-level SwiftData persistence audits, developer workstation maintenance, and the resolution of layout and state synchronization defects on PR #9.

| 1. Repository Audit Trail: Commits, Branches & CI Evolution
| Repository Evolution: Developed initially under the project moniker Furfolio in mid-2025 before being rebranded to Pawtrackr, the project was consolidated on October 6, 2026, into the enterprise GitHub organization PWM_Dev alongside my-restaurant-app and the PartnershipWithMedia core platform. 
| Security & Artifact Sanitization: During the October 2026 organization transfer, the git history was sanitized to eradicate leaked tokens, artificial intelligence markers, temporary debug scripts, and external design dependencies (including orphaned UXPilot image assets). 
| The Upstream Breaking Commit (3a93e41): Titled "Rebuild the CSV and PDF exports", commit 3a93e41 refactored internal reporting routines, completely deleting InsightsViewModel.generateReportSummary() and BusinessReportService.shared. This introduced a compilation error into QualityControl/InsightsPerformanceTests.swift (lines 45–46) that blocked GitHub Actions CI from compiling unit tests on subsequent PRs.  
| The Unlimited Scalability Commit (5ac31b2): Implemented on working branch claude/youthful-hypatia-sdjzka to permanently remove the hardcoded 1,000-client view model ceiling (clientListFetchLimit = 1000) and the 5,000-client search limit. It introduced detached task background processing with isolated ModelContexts, prefetching both pets and emergencyContacts, while removing the unreferenced needsAttentionClients scanning loop that previously degraded main-thread performance.  
| The Agent Documentation Commit (15e1bbc): Formalized architectural invariants into CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md. It established explicit rules regarding detached tasks for background reads, the total ordering algorithm, stable cell identity preservation, and ensuring that stress testing harnesses are strictly isolated from release builds.  
| CodeRabbit Audit Resolution: 
| Router Isolation: The initial 0.5-second double-tap throttle was global across the router; CodeRabbit flagged that a client card tap could swallow subsequent external notifications or programmatic pushes. The guard was rewritten to be strictly tab-scoped and card-tap-scoped.  
| Combining Character Stripping: Fixed an edge-case bug where digits or plain characters followed by excessive combining marks (e.g., 1 + 500 combining accents) bypassed sanitization. The parser now strips stray combining marks on alphanumeric characters while preserving legitimate multi-codepoint emoji attributes (skin tone modifiers, zero-width joiners, and variation selectors).  
| Test Memory Isolation: Addressed an issue in the performance test loop where iterations compounded writes into a shared store. Each measurement cycle was isolated to a fresh in-memory database instance with explicit error throws.  
| 2. Workstation Diagnostics & CLI Infrastructure
| Disk Storage Reclaim: Pre-compilation simulator maintenance on macOS reclaimed 81.4 GB of disk space across 13 runtime disk images (spanning iOS, watchOS, tvOS, and xrOS) via xcrun simctl delete unavailable, accompanied by clearing Xcode DerivedData, cached archives, and user package manager caches. 
| Toolchain Integration: The development workflow incorporates the Antigravity CLI (agy v1.2.16), the Gemini CLI (v0.62.0), and the CodeRabbit CLI (coderabbit) operating under macOS terminal zsh sessions to automate reviews and manage branch synchronization. 
| 3. SwiftData Invariants & Engine Mechanics
| No @Query in View Hierarchy: ClientsViewModel does not use SwiftUI @Query property wrappers. Client records are indexed through a detached @ModelActor background fetch (ClientRepository) that transmits pre-sorted arrays of model identifiers to the main thread.  
| Model Entity Distinction: Pawtrackr contains no Appointment model entity; active shop check-ins, scheduled sessions, and groomer operational notes are managed through the Visit model.  
| Total Lexical Tiebreaking: The sorting logic in ClientListOrdering.swift was updated after static analysis identified that localizedStandardCompare could evaluate distinct UUID strings as equivalent due to its numeric-aware heuristic. UUID tiebreakers were transitioned to strict lexical string comparisons.  
| Batch Chunking Integrity: ClientStressWriter executes insertions in batches of 100 records per isolated ModelContext, purging in-memory object graphs after each chunk to prevent OS memory pressure warnings.  
| Debounce Verification: The search debounce pipeline is set to 300 ms. Fuzz tests verify that typing 60+ keystrokes at ~66 strokes/second triggers no more than 3 background database queries and produces zero main-thread stalls.

| 1. Product Evolution & Multi-Repo Ecosystem
| The application originated in June 2025 as Furfolio before being formally rebranded to Pawtrackr. It was built to solve a specific operational bottleneck: pet groomers operating in mobile vans, home salons, or metal commercial units frequently lose cellular data connectivity. Cloud-dependent business software fails or freezes in those conditions, making a local-first, zero-latency desktop and mobile app essential.
| 
| On October 6, 2026, Pawtrackr underwent a migration into the enterprise GitHub organization PWM_Dev (Partnership With Media) alongside two companion software systems:
| 
| my-restaurant-app (Louioui/restaurant.git): A real-time point-of-sale and table-management platform with custom meal preparation modifier selections, live table availability toggles, and cash/manual bank verification channels. During the migration window, a terminal conflict between branch codex/masaflow-realtime-suite and origin/Master required three dropped commits to be rescued via git branch rescued-commits and merged back into the tree. 
| PartnershipWithMedia Web Architecture: The centralized studio portfolio and web service platform. 
| Security & Repository Scrubbing: The migration across all three codebases included a security audit that stripped residual AI prompts, debug environment logs, commit leaks, and design mocks from UXPilot, decoupling apps/analytics modules to ensure clean internal compilation. 
| 2. Developer Workstation & Toolchain Diagnostics

| 3. Business Analytics & Export Engine Redesign
| On October 10, 2026, the reporting and business intelligence infrastructure in Pawtrackr underwent a complete redesign:
| 
| Export Overhaul: Deprecated granular timestamp columns (hora) in favor of operational status auditing (estado) to track service abandonment, cancellations, and client loss without cluttering spreadsheet views. 
| Streamlined CSV & PDF Metrics: Pricing, payment methods, and dish/service lines were simplified to remove modifier noise, ensuring reports are directly digestible by non-technical shop managers and accountants. 
| Walkthrough Documentation: The user-facing walkthrough guides were rewritten to present clear, simple UI/UX directions. 
| The CI Break (Commit 3a93e41): Titled "Rebuild the CSV and PDF exports", commit 3a93e41 deleted InsightsViewModel.generateReportSummary() and BusinessReportService.shared in favor of a centralized export endpoint: makeReportExports(...). Because QualityControl/InsightsPerformanceTests.swift (lines 45–46) retained references to the deleted APIs, unit test builds on subsequent PRs failed at compile time until lines 45–46 were patched to route through makeReportExports(...).  
| 4. Database Invariants & Low-Level SwiftData Mechanics
| Static analysis of Pawtrackr's persistence architecture on branch claude/youthful-hypatia-sdjzka clarified several key implementation details:
| 
| Manual Background Ingestion: ClientsViewModel does not rely on SwiftUI's @Query macro. Instead, it uses ClientRepository—a background @ModelActor that queries SQLite, filters records, and passes sorted identifier arrays back to the main thread.  
| Entity Distinctions: Pawtrackr contains no Appointment entity. Active client sessions, service pricing, check-in intervals, and shop visits are represented by the Visit model.  
| Unbounded Background Reads (Commit 5ac31b2): Previously, ClientsViewModel was artificially throttled by clientListFetchLimit = 1000 for blank queries and a 5,000-record cap for search queries. Commit 5ac31b2 replaced this with a detached background task running an isolated ModelContext that prefetches pets and emergencyContacts, executes sorting and search off the main thread, and transmits only client UUIDs to the UI. Stale tasks are cancelled on subsequent keystrokes, and the unused needsAttentionClients scanning loop was deleted.  
| Determinism in Sorting: SwiftData relationship sets (like client.pets) have no fixed sequence order. Sorting by "Pet Name" was refactored to extract the alphabetically first pet across the collection. Tiebreaking was shifted from localizedStandardCompare to strict lexical UUID comparison to prevent false equality matches on unique identifiers.  
| Memory & Concurrency Isolation: Batch insertions via ClientStressWriter process records in chunks of 100 per short-lived context, clearing in-memory entity caches after each chunk to avoid memory bloat.

| Tokenized Search Engine (Client.matches)
| Search evaluates multi-word queries with full token satisfaction, case/diacritic normalization, and sanitized phone matching:
| 
| Swift
| 
| 
| 
| 
| 
| 
| extension Client {
|     func matches(searchQuery: String) -> Bool {
|         let trimmed = searchQuery.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
|         if trimmed.isEmpty { return true }
|         
|         let normalized = trimmed.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current)
|         let tokens = normalized.components(separatedBy: .whitespaces).filter { !$0.isEmpty }
|         if tokens.isEmpty { return true }
|         
|         let queryPhoneDigits = trimmed.filter { $0.isNumber }
|         let clientPhoneDigits = self.phone.filter { $0.isNumber }
|         
|         let normFirst = self.firstName.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current)
|         let normLast = self.lastName.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current)
|         let normFullForward = "\(normFirst) \(normLast)"
|         let normFullReverse = "\(normLast) \(normFirst)"
|         let normPets = self.pets.map { $0.name.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current) }
|         let normBreeds = self.pets.map { $0.breed.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current) }
|         
|         return tokens.allSatisfy { token in
|             normFirst.contains(token) ||
|             normLast.contains(token) ||
|             normFullForward.contains(token) ||
|             normFullReverse.contains(token) ||
|             (!queryPhoneDigits.isEmpty && clientPhoneDigits.contains(queryPhoneDigits)) ||
|             normPets.contains(where: { $0.contains(token) }) ||
|             normBreeds.contains(where: { $0.contains(token) })
|         }
|     }
| }
| Complete Pet Lifecycle Management
| ClientDetailView exposes EditPetSheet to modify pet records directly, while swipe actions and delete handlers unlink the pet from client.pets, delete it via modelContext.delete(pet), and commit the deletion to persistent storage.

| 4. Technical Architecture: Data Ingestion & State Machine
| The Background Fetch Pipeline (ClientRepository)
| Trigger: ClientsViewModel.loadClients() triggers on search keystroke, filter selection (Todos, Activos, Necesita atención, Información faltante), or sort toggle.  
| Cancellation: Any active fetchTask is cancelled immediately (fetchTask?.cancel()) to prevent stale queries from completing out-of-order.  
| Background Execution: A detached Task initializes an isolated ModelContext using the shared ModelContainer.  
| Relationship Prefetching: The fetch descriptor loads Client models while prefetching pets and emergencyContacts in a single pass to eliminate lazy-loading SQLite faults on the main thread.  
| In-Memory Predicate & Ordering: The background worker evaluates search tokens and executes ClientListOrdering.  
| Main Thread Hydration: The repository transmits an array of sorted [UUID] (or [PersistentIdentifier]) back to ClientsViewModel. The view model maps these IDs to local models without triggering full-table re-queries.  
| Low-Level Invariants in ClientListOrdering.swift
| Whitespace & Diacritic Stripping: Names are trimmed and compared using .folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current).  
| Nameless Record Handling: Records with empty first and last names sort to the bottom using synthetic keys (ZZZ_...).  
| Dynamic Pet Sorting: Because SwiftData sets are unordered, sorting by pet name evaluates the alphabetically first pet across each client's pets collection ($0.pets.map(\.name).sorted().first ?? "ZZZ").  
| Lexical UUID Tiebreaking: UUID tiebreaking explicitly uses lexical string comparison (uuidString < uuidString) because localizedStandardCompare treats certain alphanumeric patterns as equal, which compromised total ordering guarantees.

| C. Tokenized, Multi-Field Smart Search
| Swift
| 
| 
| 
| 
| 
| 
| // Extensions/Client+Search.swift
| extension Client {
|     func matches(searchQuery: String) -> Bool {
|         let trimmed = searchQuery.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
|         if trimmed.isEmpty { return true }
|         
|         // Normalize and tokenize by whitespace
|         let normalized = trimmed.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current)
|         let tokens = normalized.components(separatedBy: .whitespaces).filter { !$0.isEmpty }
|         if tokens.isEmpty { return true }
|         
|         // Strip non-digits for phone queries
|         let queryPhoneDigits = trimmed.filter { $0.isNumber }
|         let clientPhoneDigits = self.phone.filter { $0.isNumber }
|         
|         let normFirst = self.firstName.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current)
|         let normLast = self.lastName.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current)
|         let normFullNameForward = "\(normFirst) \(normLast)"
|         let normFullNameReverse = "\(normLast) \(normFirst)"
|         let normPets = self.pets.map { $0.name.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current) }
|         let normBreeds = self.pets.map { $0.breed.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current) }
|         
|         // Enforce universal match: ALL tokens must find at least one matching field
|         return tokens.allSatisfy { token in
|             normFirst.contains(token) ||
|             normLast.contains(token) ||
|             normFullNameForward.contains(token) ||
|             normFullNameReverse.contains(token) ||
|             (!queryPhoneDigits.isEmpty && clientPhoneDigits.contains(queryPhoneDigits)) ||
|             normPets.contains(where: { $0.contains(token) }) ||
|             normBreeds.contains(where: { $0.contains(token) })
|         }
|     }
| }

| // In ClientDetailView: Pet Deletion Handling
| extension ClientDetailView {
|     func deletePet(at offsets: IndexSet) {
|         for index in offsets {
|             let pet = client.pets[index]
|             client.pets.remove(at: index)
|             modelContext.delete(pet)
|         }
|         try? modelContext.save()
|     }
| }

| 1. Ecosystem Origins & Multi-Project Foundation (June 2025 – October 2026)
| Initial Inception as Furfolio: Development began in June 2025 under the project name Furfolio, designed as an offline-first iOS and macOS operational management application for pet grooming businesses. The design prioritized zero cloud dependence, ensuring groomers operating in metal mobile vans, basements, or remote locations without cellular reception retain uninterrupted access to client books, pet grooming notes, and service check-ins. 
| Domain Entity Architecture: Built with Swift 6, SwiftUI, SwiftData, and the MVVM architecture pattern. The database schema centers around: 
| Client: Stores contact details, addresses, and relationships. 
| Pet: Stores breed details, behavioral notes, and grooming preferences. 
| Visit: Manages operational shop appointments, service pricing, check-in intervals, and notes (Pawtrackr deliberately avoids generic Appointment models in favor of Visit).  
| Enterprise Consolidation under PWM_Dev (October 6–10, 2026): Rebranded as Pawtrackr and transferred into the enterprise GitHub organization PWM_Dev (Partnership With Media) alongside companion codebases: 
| my-restaurant-app: A real-time point-of-sale and dine-in table management platform featuring live table toggles, order modifier customizations (cilantro, salsa, extra cheese, comal/frito preparation), and cash/manual bank verification. 
| PartnershipWithMedia: Central corporate web architecture and studio showcase. 
| Repository sanitization stripped lingering design mocks (including orphaned UXPilot assets), scrubbed commit logs, pruned prototype branches, and restructured analytics modules. 
| Export Engine Redesign (October 10, 2026): Refactored reporting exports by dropping raw timestamp columns (hora) in favor of operational status tracking (estado) to audit client churn and abandoned services. Pricing, dishes, and payment columns were simplified for non-technical operators, and user walkthrough guides were rewritten for simplified onboarding.

| 4. Persistence Architecture & Concurrency Model
| Decoupled View Architecture: ClientsViewModel does not use SwiftUI @Query macros. It delegates data access to ClientRepository (a background @ModelActor), hydrating models on the @MainActor solely from pre-sorted identifier arrays.  
| Unified Single-Pass Reads: Fixed a concurrency race condition where "In Progress" visits and "All Clients" queried open Visit records independently, causing single clients to render simultaneously across multiple sections.  
| Total Ordering Determinism (ClientListOrdering.swift): Standard SwiftData relationship sets (client.pets) lack intrinsic sequence ordering. ClientListOrdering enforces total ordering by:  
| Trimming whitespace and folding diacritics/case using .folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current).  
| Pushing nameless clients to the bottom with synthetic keys (ZZZ_...).  
| Extracting the alphabetically first pet across the client's pets set when pet sorting is selected.  
| Resolving ties using creation dates followed by strict lexical UUID comparison (uuidString < uuidString) after static analysis revealed that localizedStandardCompare risked evaluating distinct UUIDs as equal.

| 6. CodeRabbit Review Audits & System Hardening
| Double-Tap Guard Scope: CodeRabbit identified that the global 0.5-second cooldown in NavigationRouter could swallow external deep links or notifications if a card tap coincided with incoming navigation. The guard was rewritten to be strictly tab-scoped and card-tap-scoped, preserving external routing paths.  
| Combining Mark Stripping in Avatars: CodeRabbit identified that digits followed by excessive combining marks (e.g., 1 + 500 combining accents) bypassed sanitization. AvatarInitials was updated to strip trailing combining marks on alphanumeric characters while preserving multi-codepoint emoji attributes (skin tones, zero-width joiners, and variation selectors).  
| Test Isolation: Addressed an issue in the performance test loop where iterations compounded writes into a shared database[cite: 1]. Each measurement cycle was isolated to a fresh in-memory database store with explicit error throws[cite: 1]. 
| Avatar Animation Fix: Removed an unpaired matchedGeometryEffect that caused recycled avatar circles to animate diagonally across the screen during grid reuse[cite: 1]. Initials extraction was forced to derive strictly from "First Last" to prevent visible initials from changing when sorting shifted[cite: 1]. 
| Layout Safeguards: Clamped phone number Label views to a maximum of two lines (lineLimit(2)), preventing 500-character phone strings or accessibility text sizes (AX5) from distorting grid cards[cite: 1].

Fixed a name selection bug where buckets 0 and 1 previously selected identical names[cite: 1].

| 3. SwiftData Schema Invariants: Relationships & Delete Rules
| To prevent database corruption and orphaned entities, Pawtrackr's persistence layer enforces explicit relationship constraints:
| 
| Swift
| 
| 
| 
| 
| 
| 
| @Model
| final class Client {
|     @Attribute(.unique) var id: UUID
|     var firstName: String
|     var lastName: String
|     var phone: String
|     var email: String
|     var address: String
|     var createdAt: Date
|     var isArchived: Bool = false
|     
|     // Explicit cascade rules prevent dangling relationships
|     @Relationship(deleteRule: .cascade, inverse: \Pet.owner)
|     var pets: [Pet] = []
|     
|     @Relationship(deleteRule: .cascade)
|     var emergencyContacts: [EmergencyContact] = []
|     
|     @Relationship(deleteRule: .cascade, inverse: \Visit.client)
|     var visits: [Visit] = []
| }
| 
| @Model
| final class Pet {
|     @Attribute(.unique) var id: UUID
|     var name: String
|     var breed: String
|     var notes: String
|     var groomingNotes: String?
|     var haircutSpecs: String?
|     var isArchived: Bool = false
|     
|     var owner: Client?
| }
| Cascade Rules on Child Entities: Deleting a Client automatically purges all attached Pet and Visit records, preventing dangling foreign-key references in the underlying SQLite database. 
| Isolated AppNotification Lifecycle: AppNotification entities are deliberately not linked via foreign keys to Client or Visit. This ensures that clearing the notification inbox ("Borrar todo") removes notification logs without inadvertently affecting client profiles or appointment histories.
