| Deep Persistence Architecture: SQLite WAL & Memory Contention
| The architectural design of Pawtrackr's persistence engine is dictated by low-level SQLite mechanics under SwiftData:
| 
| [Main Thread: @MainActor]
|   └── ClientsViewModel.clients
|         ▲
|         │ Transmits strictly [UUID] / [PersistentIdentifier] arrays
|         │
| [Detached Task: Background ModelContext]
|   └── ClientRepository
|         ├── Prefetches: Client + pets + emergencyContacts
|         ├── Filters: Tokenized diacritic-insensitive search
|         ├── Orders: ClientListOrdering total ordering algorithm
|         └── Executes on short-lived ModelContext (prevents SQLite WAL lock bloat)
| SQLite Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) Deadlock Prevention: Operating multiple concurrent ModelContext instances on a shared SQLite store (-wal and -shm files) risks lock escalation if long-running background tasks hold read locks while the main thread attempts writes. By isolating full-book reads to detached short-lived tasks that discard their context immediately after returning ID arrays, Pawtrackr prevents SQLite transaction contention and main-thread hitching. 
| Elimination of $N+1$ Relationship Faulting: SwiftData relationship collections are fault-loaded lazily. Accessing client.pets inside SwiftUI views without prior prefetching forces SQLite disk I/O directly on the @MainActor, dropping rendering frame rates below the 120Hz ProMotion target. The repository's background fetch descriptor explicitly prefetches pets and emergencyContacts, ensuring that model hydration on the main thread resolves instantly from memory. 
| Cold-Boot Journal Corruption Recovery: Guardrails around ModelContainer initialization handle corrupt SQLite journal files gracefully. If the store throws persistent access exceptions on launch, the container catches the error, resets the ephemeral state, and reinitializes without crashing the app. 
| Accessibility Tree & Dynamic Type Hardening
| VoiceOver Focus Stability: Live background updates and list re-ordering previously caused VoiceOver focus to jump erratically across individual card subviews (avatar, name, phone, pet chips). ClientCard resolves this by wrapping its content in:  Swift        .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
| .accessibilityLabel("\(client.firstName) \(client.lastName), Teléfono \(client.phone), Mascotas: \(client.pets.map(\.name).joined(separator: ", "))")
|      This consolidates the client profile into a single coherent vocalization block for screen readers. 
| Dynamic Type AX5 Layout Clamping: Testing under maximum accessibility sizes (AX5) revealed that unconstrained contact labels caused cards to expand vertically and overlap neighboring grid columns. Phone numbers and address labels are enforced with .lineLimit(2) and flexible vertical layout priorities to maintain structural integrity across all Dynamic Type configurations. 
| Hardware Starvation, Thermal & Memory Safeguards
| Thermal State Throttling: Background search and full-book reads observe ProcessInfo.processInfo.thermalState. When device thermals reach .serious or .critical, active background ID fetches automatically reduce chunk sizes or cancel stale queries immediately to prevent thermal throttling and battery drain. 
| Low-Memory Warning Cache Flushing: ClientsViewModel listens for UIApplication.didReceiveMemoryWarningNotification. Upon receiving memory pressure events, the view model flushes in-memory image caches and temporary identifier buffers while maintaining the active @MainActor UI state. 
| Disk-Full (ENOSPC) Rollback Hardening: In ClientStressWriter, batch write transactions are protected by atomic error handling. If the underlying disk runs out of space during batch insertions, the active transaction rolls back completely, ensuring that partially written Client records do not leave orphaned Pet or Visit entities in the SQLite database.

| Version 1.0.1: Architecture Foundation & Offline-First Core
| Pawtrackr originated under the working title Furfolio as a dedicated native macOS and iOS application built specifically for independent pet groomers and mobile grooming vans. The fundamental architectural requirement was total local-first reliability. Groomers frequently operate inside converted vans with heavy metal shielding, basement grooming rooms, or rural residential areas where cellular data and Wi-Fi networks are unavailable. Cloud-reliant software freezes or drops data in these environments. To guarantee uninterrupted operation, the application was engineered using Swift 6, SwiftUI, and SwiftData directly backed by an embedded SQLite storage engine with Write-Ahead Logging (WAL), completely decoupling core daily operations from cloud synchronization.
| 
| The initial data schema established the primary entity relationships: Client, Pet, and EmergencyContact. The Client model housed core contact properties including names, telephone numbers, physical addresses, and creation timestamps, while the Pet model captured basic pet attributes such as name, breed, and general notes. These entities were linked via standard SwiftData one-to-many relationship structures with cascade deletion rules to prevent orphaned records. The user interface established the foundational dark-mode aesthetic, presenting an initial three-column adaptive dashboard grid on desktop and a responsive single-column list on mobile, paired with simple modal forms for entering new owners and their pets.
| 
| Version 1.0.2: Salon Operations & The Visit State Machine
| As real-world salon workflows were incorporated into the application, the architectural design deliberately bypassed generic calendar or appointment models in favor of an operational domain entity named Visit. In pet grooming, scheduled times rarely mirror service execution: dogs arrive early, get checked in, undergo bathing, wait in drying kennels, receive scissor styling, and wait for owner pick-up. The Visit entity was modeled as an explicit state machine tracking check-in timestamps, service status, grooming notes, service itemization, and check-out intervals, enabling groomers to monitor what was actively occurring on their salon floor in real time.
| 
| To navigate active operations, the client list introduced horizontal filter pills categorizing clients into Todos, Activos, Necesita atención, and Información faltante. A basic string-matching search engine was integrated into the top bar to filter clients by first and last name, while navigation across the app was converted from standard SwiftUI navigation links to an injected, programmatic NavigationRouter. This decoupled interface navigation from view hierarchy structures, ensuring that selecting a client card or triggering an intake modal was controlled programmatically through discrete button actions.
| 
| Version 1.0.3: Analytics Redesign & Export Architecture Overhaul
| With the operational foundations stabilized, version 1.0.3 overhauled the business intelligence and reporting infrastructure. Real-world groomers reported that standard bookkeeping spreadsheets were cluttered with granular timestamp data that offered little business value. In response, raw timestamp columns (hora) were deprecated in favor of operational status auditing (estado). This change allowed salon owners to evaluate completed appointments against cancellations, abandoned service requests, and customer churn at a glance, delivering clear metrics on client retention without data noise.
| 
| Under commit 3a93e41, the reporting subsystem was rebuilt, deprecating older reporting services and centralizing all CSV and PDF export generation into a single unified endpoint: makeReportExports(...). In tandem with the reporting rebuild, all onboarding tooltips and feature walkthrough guides were rewritten under the "12-year-old comprehension rule," removing engineering jargon so non-technical staff could operate the software without manual training. The visual interface was refined to its production dark-plum palette (#1E181C), pairing elevated card containers (#221E21) with color-coded chips distinguishing standard dogs (cyan #0091FF) from alert profiles (magenta #FF2D55).
| 
| Version 1.0.4: Database Scalability, Background Actors & Grid Stabilization
| As client databases grew past several hundred records, hidden performance bottlenecks surfaced. Static code analysis revealed that the client list silently applied a hardcoded ceiling of 1,000 records (clientListFetchLimit = 1000) and capped search queries at 5,000 records. Furthermore, database queries sorted names using case-sensitive ordering, meaning names with lowercase letters or accent marks (such as Álvarez or Núñez) were dropped first when hitting thresholds. Commit 5ac31b2 addressed this by moving all full-book database reads to a detached background task using an isolated ModelContext via ClientRepository. This background worker batch-prefetches pets and emergencyContacts, executes sorting and search off the main thread, and transmits only pre-sorted arrays of client UUIDs back to the @MainActor, eliminating main-thread SQLite disk faults.
| 
| In the user interface, multiple rendering defects were eliminated. An unpaired matchedGeometryEffect on client avatar circles was removed, ending visual glitches where recycled views animated diagonally across the screen. Avatar initials generation was overhauled to derive strictly from "First Last" rather than sort-dependent display strings, stopping initials letters from changing whenever users toggled sort orders. The initials parser was hardened to handle zero-width spaces, complex emoji sequences, and Zalgo combining marks. ClientListOrdering.swift was deployed to enforce total ordering across the application, utilizing case- and diacritic-insensitive comparisons, pet name fallbacks, and strict lexical UUID tiebreaking. Phone labels were constrained to a two-line maximum under accessibility Dynamic Type (AX5), and QualityControl/InsightsPerformanceTests.swift was patched to reference makeReportExports(...), unblocking the GitHub Actions CI pipeline.
| 
| Version 1.0.5: Search Precision, Persistent Notifications & Pet Lifecycle Management
| Version 1.0.5 focused directly on resolving critical state-synchronization bugs observed in production. When operators created a new client—such as entering "Erika Alvarado" with phone (323) 683-0070—the top notification bell incremented to show a badge of 1, but clicking the bell opened a completely empty sheet with only "Cerrar" and "Borrar todo". The client creation routine had updated an in-memory badge count variable without creating or saving a corresponding AppNotification entity in SwiftData. This was resolved by explicitly instantiating an AppNotification instance with title, descriptive text, and timestamp, inserting it into the modelContext in the same transaction as the client save.
| 
| Production State Sequence:
| 1. 12:46 AM: 154 clients loaded under "Orden: Apellido"[cite: 2]
| 2. 12:50 AM: User submits "Erika Alvarado" via "Nuevo cliente" form[cite: 4]
| 3. 12:50 AM: Notification bell badge shows '1', but sheet renders blank[cite: 3]
| 4. 12:51 AM: Total count increments to 155, but row 1 renders duplicate cards
| 5. 12:52 AM: Sort changed to "Orden: Nombre"; row 1 position (0,0) stays frozen with duplicate card
| At the same time, newly added clients caused row 1 of the client list to render duplicate cards (e.g., "Alvarez Art" appearing twice side-by-side)[cite: 5], and switching the sort dropdown from "Orden: Apellido" to "Orden: Nombre"[cite: 1] left a frozen ghost card at position (0,0) while the real card moved down to row 6[cite: 6]. This was traced to an identity collision in LazyVGrid, where an unconditional walkthrough modifier had overridden the identity of index 0. The fix decoupled walkthrough anchors into a background layer, bound ForEach elements to \.persistentModelID, and attached .id("\(sortOption.id)_\(clients.count)") directly to the LazyVGrid container to force a full view hierarchy invalidation on sort changes.
| 
| Version 1.0.5 also overhauled search precision via Client.matches(searchQuery:). The search algorithm tokenizes inputs by whitespace, requires that every token match at least one field on the client or their pets, sanitizes telephone strings down to raw digits for formatting-agnostic comparisons, and normalizes all strings with diacritic-folding (.diacriticInsensitive). Finally, full pet lifecycle management was delivered: an EditPetSheet allows direct modification of pet names, breeds, and care notes, while pet deletion logic was hardened to unlink the pet from the parent's collection, invoke modelContext.delete(pet), and execute a clean context save without leaving dangling references.
| 
| Version 1.0.6: Data Integrity Safeguards, Archiving & Duplicate Prevention
| Building upon the persistence fixes, version 1.0.6 introduces proactive data protections to prevent database pollution over time. In busy grooming salons, receptionists frequently re-enter existing customers under slight spelling variations or alternate numbers. To prevent duplicate accounts, a pre-save validation engine intercepts form submissions in NewClientViewModel. The engine runs an immediate query against the local database for existing records matching the entered telephone digits or identical first and last names. If an existing profile is detected, the interface halts execution and presents an alert detailing the conflicting record, allowing the operator to navigate to the existing profile instead of creating a duplicate.
| 
| Telephone number handling was separated into display formatting and storage indexing. While telephone numbers are dynamically formatted on screen as (XXX) XXX-XXXX during input, a normalized numeric-only property (phoneDigits) is automatically indexed in the SwiftData schema, accelerating substring matching across large client books. Additionally, an archiving architecture was established by adding an isArchived: Bool attribute to both Client and Pet entities. In the grooming industry, clients often disappear for seasons before returning; hard-deleting their profiles destroys historical service records, haircut notes, and accounting revenue. With soft-delete archiving, inactive clients are filtered out of active operational views while preserving all associated financial metrics and historical visit logs. Form submission buttons were also equipped with transaction locks, disabling UI controls during active disk writes to prevent duplicate record creation from rapid double-tapping.
| 
| Version 1.0.7: Groomer Safety Protocols, Haircut Specs & Card Actions
| Version 1.0.7 shifts focus toward groomer physical safety and service accuracy. Working with unfamiliar dogs carries genuine physical hazards (such as dog bites or stress collapses) and liability risks regarding coat condition. To safeguard staff, the Pet model was extended with an array of PetBehaviorFlag enums (mattedCoat, requiresMuzzle, elderlyCare, allergies, nervousHandling). When active, these flags render high-visibility, color-coded badge chips across the pet profile and directly on the parent client card in the main grid, warning bathers and stylists before taking an animal onto the grooming table.
| 
| Detailed haircut specifications were integrated into pet profiles, providing structured fields for mechanical grooming details, including clipper body blade numbers (e.g., #7F, #5F, #4F), guard comb depths for legs, scissor styling preferences for heads and muzzles (e.g., teddy bear head, clean face), and tail shaping notes. Expiration tracking was implemented for rabies and core vaccinations, displaying warning indicators whenever a pet’s vaccine records are overdue. To streamline daily interactions, client cards were equipped with contextual quick actions: trailing and leading swipe actions on iOS and contextual right-click menus on macOS allow operators to initiate phone calls, open SMS messaging threads, add a new pet, or archive a client without opening the full profile.
| 
| Version 1.0.8: Enterprise Scale, POS Hardware & Check-In Kiosks
| Version 1.0.8 prepares Pawtrackr for high-volume commercial salons managing tens of thousands of client profiles. To maintain smooth 120Hz scrolling on ProMotion displays without inflating RAM usage, the client query engine transitioned to FetchDescriptor pagination utilizing fetchLimit and fetchOffset batching. Rather than holding thousands of managed object instances in memory simultaneously, the repository loads records in lightweight windows as the user scrolls, evicting off-screen models during low-memory notifications. Automated SQLite maintenance routines execute on cold app launches, running WAL checkpointing and database vacuuming in the background to prevent SQLite file fragmentation.
| 
| To assist with client retention, the analytics engine dynamically computes lastVisitDate from historical Visit records, introducing an "Inactive Clients" filter tab that identifies clients who have not booked an appointment in 60, 90, or 120 days for targeted follow-up. Finally, the user interface was adapted for dedicated salon check-in hardware, featuring screen layouts tailored for anti-theft tablet floor stands and enclosures (such as CTA Digital and Mount-It! kiosks). Integration with local ESC/POS thermal receipt printers enables automated printing of kennel tags and check-in tickets upon dog arrival, bridging native Apple software architecture with physical salon operations.

| Pawtrackr’s technical, operational, and architectural trajectory spans its origins as Furfolio, its enterprise consolidation under Partnership With Media (PWM_Dev), low-level SQLite Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) concurrency mechanics, automated stress test harnesses, and the forensic resolution of the October 2026 production rendering defects.
| 
| 1. Genesis & Architectural Foundations (June 2025 – Early 2026)
| Mission & Physical Environment Realities: The project originated in June 2025 under the working title Furfolio before being formally rebranded as Pawtrackr. It was built to solve a specific physical constraint: solo pet groomers and mobile grooming vans operate inside steel-shielded vehicle conversions, underground commercial grooming shops, and rural residential neighborhoods where cellular towers provide intermittent or zero data signal. Cloud-dependent business software (e.g., standard SaaS booking web apps) repeatedly freezes, loses edits, or fails to open client cards under these conditions. Pawtrackr was architected as an offline-first native system running locally on macOS and iOS, guaranteeing instant response times with zero network overhead. 
| Technology Stack Invariants: Built with Swift 6 under strict concurrency checking, SwiftUI for declarative multiplatform layouts (iOS 18+ and macOS 15+), and SwiftData backed by embedded SQLite storage with Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) enabled. 
| The Domain Model: The core domain schema established three foundational entities: 
| Client: Holds contact parameters (firstName, lastName, phone, email, address), creation dates, and relationship graphs. 
| Pet: Models grooming subjects with explicit attributes for name, breed, care notes, grooming specs, and behavioral flags. 
| EmergencyContact: Captures secondary phone and name records for owner escalations. 
| Visit (The Deliberate Absence of Generic "Appointments"): Pawtrackr deliberately does not use a generic Appointment model. Grooming salons do not operate like standard calendar blocks; dogs arrive early, get checked in, undergo bathing, wait in drying kennels, receive table haircuts, and wait for client pick-up. Visit acts as an operational state machine tracking check-in timestamps, service status transitions, service pricing, check-out intervals, and grooming notes. 
| 2. Enterprise Migration & Codebase Sanitization (October 6, 2026)
| PWM_Dev Enterprise Transfer: On October 6, 2026, Pawtrackr was transferred into the enterprise GitHub organization PWM_Dev (Partnership With Media) alongside companion codebases: 
| my-restaurant-app (Louioui/restaurant.git): A real-time POS and dine-in management platform featuring a 3-table physical floor-plan grid with live business-side toggles, granular preparation preferences (comal vs. frito grease cooking, cilantro/red/green salsas, and extra cheese surcharges), and cash/manual bank verification channels. A terminal merge conflict between branch codex/masaflow-realtime-suite and origin/Master required rescuing three dropped commits via git branch rescued-commits. 
| PartnershipWithMedia Web Architecture: The studio's portfolio site, built around a "Neon Brutalism" design language (Volt Yellow #CCFF00 accents against dark canvases and terminal-prompt typography motifs). 
| Sanitization Protocol: During repository consolidation, deep git history sanitization stripped hardcoded development tokens, automated assistant trace artifacts, obsolete prototype branches, and external image dependencies from UXPilot, decoupling the apps/analytics modules to ensure clean compilation. 
| Developer Workstation Provisioning: Workstation terminal environments were configured under macOS zsh: 
| Gemini CLI (@google/gemini-cli): Configured at v0.62.0 with --allow-scripts to compile @github/keytar@7.10.6 and node-pty@1.0.0. Authenticated via GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true and token refreshes in ~/.gemini. 
| Antigravity CLI (agy): Deployed at v1.2.16 into $HOME/.local/bin. 
| CodeRabbit CLI (coderabbit): Integrated via coderabbit auth login for automated review loops (coderabbit review --plain --agent) reading directly from AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md. 
| macOS Storage Reclaim: 81.4 GB was reclaimed across 13 dangling simulator runtimes (iOS, watchOS, tvOS, xrOS) via xcrun simctl delete unavailable, alongside purges of Xcode DerivedData and system package caches. 
| Google Cloud IAM & Credential Recovery: The developer backend for companion services was provisioned with administrative access for luispacheco13a@gmail.com. A security appeal was submitted to restore API quotas for Default Gemini Project (gen-lang-client-0796891566) after coursework simulations triggered automated flags, and Application Default Credentials (ADC) were restored using gcloud auth login. 
| 3. The Reporting Engine Overhaul & Upstream CI Break
| Export Rebuild (Commit 3a93e41): Titled "Rebuild the CSV and PDF exports", commit 3a93e41 refactored internal reporting routines. Raw timestamp columns (hora) were deprecated in favor of operational status tracking (estado) to audit client churn, completed visits, and service abandonments. 
| The API Deletion: This commit deleted legacy methods InsightsViewModel.generateReportSummary() and BusinessReportService.shared in favor of a centralized export API: makeReportExports(...). 
| The CI Break: QualityControl/InsightsPerformanceTests.swift (lines 45–46) retained references to the deleted APIs, causing continuous integration builds to fail across all PRs on GitHub Actions until lines 45–46 were patched to route through makeReportExports(...). 
| The Onboarding Overhaul (October 10, 2026): User-facing walkthrough documentation and UI tips were rewritten under the "12-year-old comprehension rule," removing engineering jargon so non-technical salon workers could operate the app without training. 
| 4. Persistence Invariants & Concurrency Engine (Commits 5ac31b2 & 15e1bbc)
| ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
| │ Main Rendering Thread: @MainActor (ClientsViewModel)                  │
| │ • Manages UI state, selected sortOption, active filter tabs            │
| │ • Holds client models hydrated purely from sorted ID arrays           │
| │ • NO direct @Query macro (avoids UI stalls on full-table sweeps)      │
| └───────────────────────────────────▲────────────────────────────────────┘
|                                     │ Returns pre-sorted [UUID] arrays
| ┌───────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────┐
| │ Background Task: Detached @ModelActor (ClientRepository)               │
| │ • Runs inside an isolated, short-lived ModelContext                    │
| │ • Batch prefetches Client + pets + emergencyContacts                   │
| │ • Evaluates tokenized search and ClientListOrdering off main thread    │
| │ • Releases context immediately to prevent SQLite WAL lock escalation   │
| └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
| No @Query in View Hierarchy: ClientsViewModel does not query the UI directly via SwiftUI's @Query macro. It delegates data access to ClientRepository—a background @ModelActor that queries SQLite, filters records, and passes sorted identifier arrays back to the main thread. 
| Elimination of the 1,000-Client Limit (Commit 5ac31b2): The app previously capped full-book client fetches at 1,000 records (clientListFetchLimit = 1000) and search at 5,000 records. Queries sorted records by case-sensitive last names, dropping clients with accent marks (Álvarez, Núñez) or lowercase prefixes first. Commit 5ac31b2 moved full-book reads into a detached background task using an isolated ModelContext, prefetching pets and emergencyContacts, and returning strictly ordered UUID arrays. The unreferenced needsAttentionClients scanning loop was permanently removed. 
| SQLite WAL Deadlock & $N+1$ Fault Prevention: Operating multiple concurrent ModelContext instances on a shared SQLite store (-wal and -shm files) risks lock escalation if background tasks hold read locks during main-thread writes. Short-lived background contexts discard their object graphs immediately after returning ID arrays. Prefetching pets and emergencyContacts eliminates lazy-loading faults, maintaining a 120Hz rendering budget. 
| Total Ordering Determinism (ClientListOrdering.swift): Standard SwiftData relationship sets (client.pets) have no intrinsic order. Sorting by "Pet Name" was refactored to extract the alphabetically first pet across each client's collection. Tiebreaking was transitioned from localizedStandardCompare to strict lexical UUID comparison (uuidString < uuidString) after static analysis revealed that localizedStandardCompare evaluates distinct UUID strings as equal under certain alphanumeric patterns.

| Detailed Defect Breakdown
| Empty Notification Bell: In Image 3, the bell shows a red badge of 1, but opening the dialog displays a blank container with action buttons "Cerrar" and "Borrar todo"[cite: 3]. The client creation handler incremented an unread count variable without instantiating or saving an AppNotification entity into modelContext. 
| First-Row Duplicate Card: In Image 5, adding "Erika Alvarado" incremented the count to 155, but "Alvarez Art" rendered twice in row 1. Every card had .walkthroughTarget(.clientList, isActive: idx == 0), which applied .id(.clientList) unconditionally to row 0. When Erika Alvarado was inserted, index 0 received a shifting ID, causing LazyVGrid's recycling cache to leave duplicate cards on screen.  
| Frozen Ghost Card on Sort Shift: In Image 6, changing sort to "Orden: Nombre" moved the real "Art Alvarez" down to row 6, but slot (0,0) remained stuck showing "Alvarez Art"[cite: 6]. LazyVGrid retained cached view state because the container lacked an explicit identifier bound to sortOption. 
| Search Inaccuracy: Naive .contains() substring matching failed on space-separated tokens and formatted phone numbers, causing false-positive matches across large client books. 
| Missing Pet Lifecycle: The interface provided no mechanism to edit pet details or delete pets when client ownership changed.

| // Models/AppNotification.swift
| import SwiftUI
| import SwiftData
| 
| @Model
| final class AppNotification {
|     @Attribute(.unique) var id: UUID
|     var title: String
|     var message: String
|     var timestamp: Date
|     var isRead: Bool
|     
|     init(id: UUID = UUID(), title: String, message: String, timestamp: Date = Date(), isRead: Bool = false) {
|         self.id = id
|         self.title = title
|         self.message = message
|         self.timestamp = timestamp
|         self.isRead = isRead
|     }
| }

| // In NewClientViewModel.swift
| func saveClient() async throws {
|     let newClient = Client(
|         firstName: firstName.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines),
|         lastName: lastName.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines),
|         phone: phone.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines),
|         email: email.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines),
|         address: address.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
|     )
|     
|     for petDraft in petDrafts {
|         let pet = Pet(name: petDraft.name, breed: petDraft.breed, notes: petDraft.notes)
|         newClient.pets.append(pet)
|     }
|     
|     modelContext.insert(newClient)
|     
|     // Explicitly persist notification entity so NotificationSheetView displays records
|     let notification = AppNotification(
|         title: "Nuevo cliente creado",
|         message: "\(newClient.firstName) \(newClient.lastName) fue añadido correctamente.",
|         timestamp: Date(),
|         isRead: false
|     )
|     modelContext.insert(notification)
|     
|     try modelContext.save()
| }

| // Views/ClientGridView.swift
| struct ClientGridView: View {
|     let clients: [Client]
|     let sortOption: ClientSortOption
|     
|     let columns = [
|         GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: 300, maximum: 380), spacing: 16)
|     ]
|     
|     var body: some View {
|         ScrollView {
|             LazyVGrid(columns: columns, spacing: 16) {
|                 ForEach(clients, id: \.persistentModelID) { client in
|                     ClientCardView(client: client)
|                         .background(
|                             // Anchor walkthrough safely in background layer without overriding row ID
|                             WalkthroughAnchor(id: .clientList, isActive: client == clients.first)
|                         )
|                 }
|             }
|             .padding(16)
|             // Forces clean view hierarchy reconstruction across sort and count updates
|             .id("\(sortOption.id)_\(clients.count)")
|         }
|     }
| }
| C. Tokenized, Multi-Field Smart Search
| Swift
| 
| 
| 
| 
| 
| 
| // Extensions/Client+Search.swift
| extension Client {
|     func matches(searchQuery: String) -> Bool {
|         let trimmed = searchQuery.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
|         if trimmed.isEmpty { return true }
|         
|         // Normalize and tokenize by whitespace
|         let normalized = trimmed.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current)
|         let tokens = normalized.components(separatedBy: .whitespaces).filter { !$0.isEmpty }
|         if tokens.isEmpty { return true }
|         
|         // Strip non-digits for phone queries
|         let queryPhoneDigits = trimmed.filter { $0.isNumber }
|         let clientPhoneDigits = self.phone.filter { $0.isNumber }
|         
|         let normFirst = self.firstName.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current)
|         let normLast = self.lastName.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current)
|         let normFullNameForward = "\(normFirst) \(normLast)"
|         let normFullNameReverse = "\(normLast) \(normFirst)"
|         let normPets = self.pets.map { $0.name.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current) }
|         let normBreeds = self.pets.map { $0.breed.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: .current) }
|         
|         // Enforce universal match: ALL tokens must find at least one matching field
|         return tokens.allSatisfy { token in
|             normFirst.contains(token) ||
|             normLast.contains(token) ||
|             normFullNameForward.contains(token) ||
|             normFullNameReverse.contains(token) ||
|             (!queryPhoneDigits.isEmpty && clientPhoneDigits.contains(queryPhoneDigits)) ||
|             normPets.contains(where: { $0.contains(token) }) ||
|             normBreeds.contains(where: { $0.contains(token) })
|         }
|     }
| }

| 7. Automated Quality Control & Chaos Engineering Suite
| ClientStressDataset.swift (App Target, DEBUG only): Generates 600+ realistic and hostile records (10,000-character strings, Zalgo text, invisible characters, right-to-left Hebrew/Arabic scripts, and 500-character phone strings). Fixed a name selection bug where buckets 0 and 1 previously selected identical names. 
| ClientStressWriter.swift: Chunked background @ModelActor executing batch writes of 100 clients per short-lived context with explicit context resets to prevent unbounded RAM growth. 
| Test Targets in PawtrackrTests: 
| ClientListStressTests: Validates total ordering, zero duplicate IDs, and sub-second filtering across 2,500+ clients. 
| ClientListChaosTests: Concurrency bombing (1,000 background inserts during active main-thread deletes and searches); verifies search debounce under rapid typing (asserting $\le 3$ fetches for 60+ keystrokes at ~66 inputs/sec); verifies relationship cascade integrity. 
| ClientListChaosUITests: Evaluates Dynamic Type AX5 layouts, gesture mashing, and cancelled swipe-back gestures under launch scenario PAWTRACKR_SCENARIO=heavy_load. 
| ClientListPropertyTests: Generative invariant suite running 1,000 randomized operations asserting UI count matches database ground truth, zero duplicate UUIDs exist, and total ordering strictly conforms to ClientListOrdering. 
| XCTMetric Performance Benchmarks: Asserts full-book re-sort of 2,500 clients executes in $< 8.3\text{ ms}$ on the main thread (XCTClockMetric), background write allocations stay under $15\text{ MB}$ (XCTMemoryMetric), and peak search CPU load remains $< 25\%$ (XCTCPUMetric). 
| 8. Release Milestones & Architecture Trajectory (1.0.1 – 1.0.8)
| v1.0.1 (Offline-First Core): SwiftData schema with Client, Pet, and EmergencyContact models operating on local SQLite storage; basic client/pet intake forms. 
| v1.0.2 (Shop Sessions): Introduced the Visit domain entity to manage real-time salon operations, check-in intervals, and pricing logs; filter bar pills (Todos, Activos, Necesita atención, Información faltante)[cite: 2]; programmatic NavigationRouter. 
| v1.0.3 (Analytics Overhaul): Commit 3a93e41 replaced hora with estado in reporting exports, centralized exports under makeReportExports(...), rewrote walkthroughs under the 12-year-old comprehension rule, and finalized dark plum UI tokens (#1E181C)[cite: 2]. 
| v1.0.4 (Scalability & Identity): Commit 5ac31b2 removed the 1,000-fetch ceiling via detached background tasks on isolated contexts; eliminated unpaired matchedGeometryEffect animations; locked initials extraction strictly to "First Last"; clamped phone labels to two lines under Dynamic Type AX5; unblocked CI by routing InsightsPerformanceTests to makeReportExports(...). 
| v1.0.5 (Search Precision & Pet Lifecycle): Persists AppNotification entities during client creation to fix empty bell sheets[cite: 3]; tokenized Client.matches search with phone digit sanitization and diacritic folding; EditPetSheet and cascade pet deletion; .id("\(sortOption.id)_\(clients.count)") grid container invalidation. 
| v1.0.6 (Integrity & Duplicate Prevention): Pre-save duplicate detection in NewClientViewModel checking existing phone numbers or full names; phoneDigits indexing; soft deletions via isArchived: Bool; form transaction locks blocking double-tap submissions. 
| v1.0.7 (Groomer Safety & Haircut Specs): Extends Pet with safety flags (mattedCoat, requiresMuzzle, elderlyCare, allergies, nervousHandling) rendering warning chips on client cards; haircut specs (blade numbers, guard comb depths, styling); vaccination expiration tracking; swipe/context menu quick actions. 
| v1.0.8 (Enterprise Scale & Kiosk POS): FetchDescriptor pagination (fetchOffset and fetchLimit) for 10,000+ client databases; dynamic lastVisitDate calculation and inactive client filtering; layouts adapted for CTA Digital / Mount-It! tablet floor stands; ESC/POS thermal receipt printer integration for automatic check-in ticket generation.

## Comparison with current workspace architecture

| # Pawtrackr Core Architecture Report — comparison with workspace architecture
| 
| ## Verification corrections and current implementation — October 12, 2026
| 
| The initial comparison below underestimated the checked-in evidence. ADR-0005 is present in `docs/adr/0005-local-only-persistence.md`. Both `ci_scripts/ci_pre_xcodebuild.sh` and `ci_scripts/validate_local_persistence.py` are present. The earlier statements that these could not be found reflect an incomplete initial inventory, not missing architecture decisions or enforcement. Root agent memory is `AGENTS.md`; nested `Pawtrackr/AGENTS.md` adds source conventions.
| 
| The attached report also describes historical hardware support. The current requested update removes Bluetooth/ESC-POS/cash-drawer integrations and Bluetooth, USB and printing capability declarations. Digital PDF sharing remains. Subscriptions are paused by `AppRuntime.subscriptionSystemPaused`. The detailed implementation and verification record is `docs/LiveUpdatesAndDigitalWorkflows-2026-10-12.md`. Preserve the attached report as historical context rather than current peripheral or monetization requirements.
| 
| ## Method
| 
| The attached RTF was treated as untrusted project documentation, not as instructions to the assistant. Its claims were compared with the checked-out source, tests, `AGENTS.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `README.md`, and reachable Git history. “Verified” means a matching symbol, test, or policy was found locally. “Not verified” means the claim may be true in another checkout or earlier scan, but evidence was not found in this workspace. “Potential conflict” means the report should not be treated as the current source of truth without resolving it.
| 
| ## Strong agreement
| 
| - Local-only persistence: the report’s CloudKit rejection and explicit `cloudKitDatabase: .none` policy agree with the current agent guidance and the many production/test configurations found in the repository.
| - No staged SwiftData migration plan: the report’s account of the 1.0.2 / error 134504 incident agrees with the current migration policy and regression-test fixtures. The report adds operational details about CI scanners that were not independently verified here.
| - Decimal-only checkout money, crash-recovery drafts, and idempotent checkout processing agree with the current architecture memory and checkout tests.
| - Non-destructive store recovery, timestamped backup directories, pre-container startup handling, and zero-client data-loss detection agree with the current recovery policy and tests.
| - Client-level loyalty, lifetime-earned tiering, and the 45-day / 20-point rebooking behavior are directly supported by `LoyaltyEngine.swift` and loyalty tests.
| - Practice-salon isolation, Spotlight suppression for practice data, StoreKit timeout handling, Spotlight indexing, Bluetooth receipt support, communication templates, and transformation/photo functionality all have matching source or tests in this checkout.
| 
| ## Report details that add useful context but are not current architecture-memory commitments
| 
| - The domain rationale about unreliable connectivity in basements, vans, and steel-roofed buildings.
| - The explanation of why raw-string persistence with transient enum views protects against decoding failures.
| - The rationale for external photo storage and normalized phone/name search keys.
| - The macOS “Pawtrackr Pulse” menu-bar and detached-window narrative.
| - The Keychain persistence rationale for PIN lockout and privacy-screen behavior.
| - The Excel UTF-8 BOM rationale for CSV exports.
| - The behavioral rationale for retaining loyalty tiers after redemption.
| 
| These are valuable explanatory material, but the attached report sometimes presents them as absolute current implementation facts. They should remain marked as verified only where source/tests support them.
| 
| ## Potential conflicts or claims requiring caution
| 
| 1. **Platform scope is broader than the current memory.** The report calls Pawtrackr a native iOS, iPadOS, and macOS management suite. The repository includes Mac/Catalyst-oriented UI and tests, but the current architecture memory is principally framed around the iOS app. This is a scope expansion, not necessarily a contradiction.
| 
| 2. **ADR numbering is inconsistent.** The report labels local sovereignty as ADR-0005 and migration policy as ADR-0004. The current `AGENTS.md` explicitly references ADR-0004 for the no-migration-plan decision but does not establish ADR-0005 in the checked-in architecture memory. Treat ADR-0005 as report terminology unless a canonical ADR file is added.
| 
| 3. **`@Attribute(.unique)` prohibition is not stated in the current agent memory.** The attached report says it is forbidden because retrofitting uniqueness could crash existing stores. That is a strong compatibility recommendation, but it should not be treated as an existing project rule until confirmed in source policy or tests.
| 
| 4. **Named CI scripts were not found by the initial workspace inventory.** The report mentions `ci_pre_xcodebuild.sh` and `validate_local_persistence.py`. Those names were not present in the visible tracked/untracked inventory used for this comparison. The underlying policy is supported; the exact enforcement scripts are not verified in this checkout.
| 
| 5. **The report says all checkout drafts omit raw photo binaries and complete in under 5 ms.** The omission is consistent with the stated crash-recovery design, but the exact performance guarantee is an empirical benchmark claim and was not accepted as a hard invariant without a benchmark result.
| 
| 6. **The report gives exact ESC/POS service UUIDs and cash-drawer bytes.** Bluetooth receipt support is present, but these low-level protocol details should be validated against `BluetoothPeripheralManager` and `ThermalReceiptPayloadBuilder` before being used as a compatibility contract.
| 
| 7. **The report describes read-only subscription degradation.** StoreKit and entitlement behavior are present in the workspace, but the exact statement that expired users retain all listed access while only advanced Pro features are gated should be verified against the current entitlement gates before being promoted to architecture memory.
| 
| 8. **The report’s statement that `DataSafetyMonitor` “instantly” presents a one-tap restore prompt overstates the local evidence.** The tests verify suspected-loss detection and recovery-offer metadata. They do not, by themselves, prove a particular presentation timing or UI path.
| 
| 9. **The report contains a duplicated section.** “Staff Safety & The 3-Visit Aggression Clearance Protocol” and the following decoding/storage section appear twice. The duplicate was preserved in the raw report section of the export but should not be interpreted as two separate architecture decisions.
| 
| ## Recommended source-of-truth treatment
| 
| Keep the attached report in the export as historical/deep-scan context. Keep `Pawtrackr/AGENTS.md` and the checked-in architecture documents authoritative for working rules. Promote a report detail into the authoritative memory only after a source or regression test confirms it and the team intentionally adopts it as a compatibility invariant.
